Determine the useful electrical power delivered to the secondary load.
Calculate the rms current drawn from the primary supply.

items.stem: Connected via slip rings to a 50 Ω load in a marine diesel-electric AC load-testing unit, an ideal coil of 100 turns and area 0.012 m² rotates at 80 Hz in a uniform 0.48 T magnetic field. What is the root-mean-square (rms) potential difference across the load?
items.workedSolution: Peak emf ε₀ = 2πfNBA = 2π(80)(100)(0.48)(0.012) = 290 V. Therefore V_rms = ε₀ / √2 = 205 V.

markScheme.criterion: Finds ε₀ = 2πfNBA and divides by √2 to obtain 205 V (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides peak emf ε₀ by 2 (confusing the ½ power factor with the 1/√2 rms voltage factor).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Stops at peak emf ε₀ = 2πfNBA without dividing by √2.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies peak emf ε₀ by √2 instead of dividing by √2.

items.stem: Within a paleoclimate ice-core Bainbridge analyser, crossed selector fields E = 9.60 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ and B₁ = 0.35 T admit potassium isotopes of charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and masses m₁ = 6.47 × 10⁻²⁶ kg and m₂ = 6.81 × 10⁻²⁶ kg through slit S into a uniform B₂ = 0.7 T magnetic sector (out of the page).

markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = m₁v / (qB₂) with chamber field B₂.
Doubles the radius difference ΔD = 2(r₂ − r₁).

parts.prompt: Calculate the common speed of the ions emerging from the velocity selector.
Determine the orbital radius r₁ of the lighter isotope in the deflection chamber.
Calculate the separation ΔD between the two isotope strike points on the detector wall.

items.stem: In a magnetic calibration run, the axial flux density perpendicular to a electromagnet pole-gap calibration search coil with 350 turns, cross-section 0.01 m², and resistance 12 Ω switches from +0.12 T to −0.0720 T during an interval of 0.08 s. What is the magnitude of the average emf induced in the coil during the reversal?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates |ΔB| across sign reversal to obtain |ε| = 8.40 V (C).

options.distractorRationale: Treats the field as dropping only to zero (ΔB = B₁) rather than reversing sign to B₂.

options.label: B

items.stem: Travelling to the left at constant velocity 8 m s⁻¹, a crossbar of resistance 1.2 Ω spans frictionless rails 0.2 m apart on a magnetohydrodynamic copper-bar carriage connected to a 1.4 Ω load in a 0.6 T field (directed out of the page). What is the terminal potential difference across the external load resistor?
items.workedSolution: ε = BLv = 0.960 V; loop current I = ε / (R + r) = 0.369 A. Terminal p.d. across load V_term = I R = 0.369 × 1.4 = 0.517 V.

markScheme.criterion: Uses V_term = BLv × R/(R + r) to obtain 0.517 V (A).

items.stem: In the camera strobe decay module shown, a capacitor of capacitance C = 300 μF is first fully charged to V₀ = 10.0 V by closing Switch A while Switches B and C remain open. Switch A is then opened and Switch B is closed so the capacitor discharges through R₁ = 60 kΩ for 12.0 s. At t = 12.0 s, while Switch B stays closed, Switch C is closed to connect R₂ = 20 kΩ in parallel with R₁ for a further 5.00 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) One farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates. (b)(i) τ₁ = R₁C = 18.00 s, so V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁) = 5.134 V ≈ 5.13 V (confirming 5.1 V). (b)(ii) R_eq = R₁R₂/(R₁+R₂) = 15.0 kΩ, giving τ₂ = R_eq C = 4.500 s ≈ 4.50 s. (b)(iii) V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂) = 1.690 V ≈ 1.69 V. (b)(iv) larger final potential difference because the time constant increases and the capacitor discharges more slowly.

markScheme.criterion: Mentions charge stored per unit potential difference (coulombs per volt).
Complete SI unit definition: capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
Evaluates stage-1 time constant τ₁ = R₁C = 18.0 s.
Correctly substitutes V₀, t₁, and τ₁ into V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁).
Shows V₁ = 5.134 V (≥3 s.f.: 5.13 V), clearly matching 5.1 V.
Combines R₁ || R₂ = 15.0 kΩ and calculates τ₂ = R_eq C = 4.50 s.
Substitutes V₁ (accepting rounded prompt value on ECF), t₂, and τ₂ into V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂).
Correct final potential difference V₂ = 1.69 V.
States correctly that V₂ would be larger (smaller/larger matching direction).
Explains via time constants in both stages: larger final potential difference because the time constant increases and the capacitor discharges more slowly.

parts.prompt: Define the farad.
parts.expectedAnswer: The farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
workingSteps: Recall the unit definition linking electric charge in coulombs and potential difference in volts.

parts.prompt: Show clearly that after discharging through R₁ alone for 12.0 s, the potential difference across the capacitor is approximately 5.1 V.
parts.expectedAnswer: 5.134 V (which rounds to 5.13 V and 5.1 V)
workingSteps: Stage 1 time constant τ₁ = R₁ C = (60 × 10³ Ω) × (300 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 18.00 s.
Substitute into V₁ = V₀ exp(−t₁ / τ₁) = 10.00 V × exp(−12 / 18.00 s).
Evaluate to 4 s.f.: V₁ = 5.134 V ≈ 5.13 V (confirming approximately 5.1 V).

parts.prompt: At the instant Switch C closes, calculate the new time constant τ₂ of the discharge circuit.
workingSteps: Combined parallel resistance R_eq = (R₁ R₂)/(R₁ + R₂) = (60 × 20) / (60 + 20) = 15.0 kΩ.
New time constant τ₂ = R_eq C = (15 × 10³ Ω) × (300 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 4.500 s ≈ 4.50 s.

parts.prompt: Calculate the potential difference V₂ across the capacitor after a further 5.00 s with both Switch B and Switch C closed.
workingSteps: Start Stage 2 decay from V₁ = 5.134 V with time constant τ₂ = 4.500 s.

parts.prompt: Without calculation, state and explain how the final potential difference V₂ would change if resistor R₁ were replaced by a larger resistor throughout the entire experiment.
parts.expectedAnswer: Replacing the first resistor with a larger resistor gives a larger final potential difference because the time constant increases and the capacitor discharges more slowly.
workingSteps: A larger resistance changes both the initial discharge time constant and the combined parallel resistance in the same direction.
Link the altered time constants in both stages to the rate of exponential decay and the remaining potential difference.

items.stem: During a charge-conservation test on an isolated laboratory capacitor bank, C₁ = 15 μF at initial voltage V₁ = 47 V is connected by closing switch S across C₂ = 45 μF (initially uncharged). What final common potential difference is established across both capacitors?
items.workedSolution: Total conserved charge Q_net = C₁V₁ + C₂V₂ = 7.05 × 10⁻⁴ C. Final parallel capacitance C_eq = 60 μF, so V_f = Q_net / (C₁ + C₂) = 11.8 V.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves net charge Q_net and divides by C₁ + C₂ to obtain 11.8 V (D).

options.distractorRationale: Divides conserved net charge by series capacitance C₁C₂/(C₁ + C₂) instead of parallel C₁ + C₂.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Assumes all initial charge from C₁ transfers onto C₂ instead of splitting across C₁ + C₂.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Takes the unweighted average (V₁ + V₂)/2 without weighting by C₁ and C₂ via charge conservation.

items.stem: Across a regulated 23 V rail in a camera strobe flash bank, capacitor C₁ (24 μF) is placed in series with capacitor C₂ (48 μF). What potential difference is developed across capacitor C₁?
items.workedSolution: Equivalent capacitance C_eq = 1.60 × 10⁻⁵ F, so series charge Q = C_eq V₀ = 3.68 × 10⁻⁴ C. Across C₁, V₁ = Q / C₁ = 15.3 V.

markScheme.criterion: Finds common series charge Q and computes V₁ = Q/C₁ = 15.3 V (B).

parts.prompt: Calculate the combined capacitance of the network between A and B in μF.
workingSteps: Parallel branch: C_p = C₂ + C₃ = 20 + 25 = 45 μF.
Series combination: C_eq = (C₁ C_p) / (C₁ + C_p) = (90 × 45) / (90 + 45) = 30.00 μF ≈ 30.0 μF.

parts.prompt: Determine the maximum safe potential difference that can be applied across A and B, stating which section reaches its voltage rating first.
parts.expectedAnswer: 75.0 V (limited by the parallel pair of capacitors)
workingSteps: In series both sections hold equal charge Q, so V ∝ 1/C; the smaller capacitance (parallel pair of capacitors) reaches 50 V first.
Maximum safe total pd V_AB,max = 50 × (1 + 45 / 90) = 75.00 V ≈ 75.0 V.

items.stem: In a sensor low-pass RC network, a 80 μF capacitor initially charged to 15 V begins discharging through a 20 kΩ resistor when switch S closes, and a sensor samples the circuit after 2.88 s. What is the potential difference across the capacitor at t = 2.88 s?
items.workedSolution: Time constant τ = RC = 1.60 s. For discharging, V_C(2.88 s) = 15 e^(−2.88/1.60) = 2.48 V.

markScheme.criterion: Finds τ = RC and evaluates V_C at t = 2.88 s to obtain 2.48 V (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides elapsed time t by half-time RC ln 2 instead of the RC time constant τ = RC in the exponent.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Applies the charging equation V₀(1 − e^(−t/RC)) instead of exponential discharge V₀e^(−t/RC).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the capacitor reaches or retains the full supply voltage V₀ instantaneously.

items.stem: During isotopic analysis on a cosmochemistry meteorite isotope separator, magnesium ions (q = +3.20 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m₁ = 3.98 × 10⁻²⁶ kg, m₂ = 4.32 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) traverse a velocity selector with E = 9.60 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ and B₁ = 0.35 T and strike a photographic detector wall after semicircular deflection in B₂ = 0.7 T (out of the page). How far from the entry slit S does the lighter isotope strike the detector wall?
items.workedSolution: v = E / B₁ = 2.74 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ and r₁ = m₁v / (qB₂) = 0.0487 m. Strike distance from slit S is D₁ = 2r₁ = 0.0975 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the separation ΔD between the two isotopes rather than the slit-to-impact distance 2r₁.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses B₁² instead of B₁B₂ in D₁ = 2m₁E/(qB₁B₂).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Reports the orbital radius r₁ rather than the semicircular chord distance D₁ = 2r₁ from slit S.

items.stem: Within a linear regenerator test track, a 2.4 Ω load terminates smooth rails separated by 0.32 m in a uniform 0.45 T field directed into the page, while a sliding rod (resistance 0.8 Ω) is driven to the right at 4 m s⁻¹.

Equates applied force to magnetic braking force F = BIL.

parts.prompt: Calculate the motional emf induced across the sliding rod.
Determine the induced current circulating around the rails.
Calculate the external pulling force magnitude required to maintain constant speed.

items.stem: In the slow-fast capacitor test unit shown, a capacitor of capacitance C = 500 μF is first fully charged to V₀ = 6.00 V by closing Switch A while Switches B and C remain open. Switch A is then opened and Switch B is closed so the capacitor discharges through R₁ = 60 kΩ for 18.0 s. At t = 18.0 s, while Switch B stays closed, Switch C is closed to connect R₂ = 30 kΩ in parallel with R₁ for a further 9.00 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) One farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates. (b)(i) τ₁ = R₁C = 30.00 s, so V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁) = 3.293 V ≈ 3.29 V (confirming 3.3 V). (b)(ii) R_eq = R₁R₂/(R₁+R₂) = 20.0 kΩ, giving τ₂ = R_eq C = 10.00 s ≈ 10.0 s. (b)(iii) V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂) = 1.339 V ≈ 1.34 V. (b)(iv) larger final potential difference because the time constant increases and the capacitor discharges more slowly.

markScheme.criterion: Mentions charge stored per unit potential difference (coulombs per volt).
Complete SI unit definition: capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
Evaluates stage-1 time constant τ₁ = R₁C = 30.0 s.
Correctly substitutes V₀, t₁, and τ₁ into V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁).
Shows V₁ = 3.293 V (≥3 s.f.: 3.29 V), clearly matching 3.3 V.
Combines R₁ || R₂ = 20.0 kΩ and calculates τ₂ = R_eq C = 10.0 s.
Substitutes V₁ (accepting rounded prompt value on ECF), t₂, and τ₂ into V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂).
Correct final potential difference V₂ = 1.34 V.
States correctly that V₂ would be larger (smaller/larger matching direction).
Explains via time constants in both stages: larger final potential difference because the time constant increases and the capacitor discharges more slowly.

parts.prompt: Define the farad.
parts.expectedAnswer: The farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
workingSteps: Recall the unit definition linking electric charge in coulombs and potential difference in volts.

parts.prompt: Show clearly that after discharging through R₁ alone for 18.0 s, the potential difference across the capacitor is approximately 3.3 V.
parts.expectedAnswer: 3.293 V (which rounds to 3.29 V and 3.3 V)
workingSteps: Stage 1 time constant τ₁ = R₁ C = (60 × 10³ Ω) × (500 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 30.00 s.
Substitute into V₁ = V₀ exp(−t₁ / τ₁) = 6.000 V × exp(−18 / 30.00 s).
Evaluate to 4 s.f.: V₁ = 3.293 V ≈ 3.29 V (confirming approximately 3.3 V).

parts.prompt: At the instant Switch C closes, calculate the new time constant τ₂ of the discharge circuit.
workingSteps: Combined parallel resistance R_eq = (R₁ R₂)/(R₁ + R₂) = (60 × 30) / (60 + 30) = 20.0 kΩ.
New time constant τ₂ = R_eq C = (20 × 10³ Ω) × (500 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 10.00 s ≈ 10.0 s.

parts.prompt: Calculate the potential difference V₂ across the capacitor after a further 9.00 s with both Switch B and Switch C closed.
workingSteps: Start Stage 2 decay from V₁ = 3.293 V with time constant τ₂ = 10.00 s.

parts.prompt: Without calculation, state and explain how the final potential difference V₂ would change if resistor R₁ were replaced by a larger resistor throughout the entire experiment.
parts.expectedAnswer: Replacing the first resistor with a larger resistor gives a larger final potential difference because the time constant increases and the capacitor discharges more slowly.
workingSteps: A larger resistance changes both the initial discharge time constant and the combined parallel resistance in the same direction.
Link the altered time constants in both stages to the rate of exponential decay and the remaining potential difference.

items.stem: After disconnecting its charging cell in an isolated laboratory capacitor bank, capacitor C₁ = 10 μF at V₁ = 47 V shares charge across switch S with C₂ = 30 μF, which is initially uncharged.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Q_net = C₁V₁ + C₂V₂ before switch closure.
Divides conserved charge from (a) by C₁ + C₂.
Subtracts final stored energy ½(C₁ + C₂)V_f² from initial stored energy.

items.stem: A potential difference of 1200 V in the source stage of a sputter-source magnetic momentum filter accelerates a singly ionised lithium ion of mass 1.16 × 10⁻²⁶ kg and charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C from rest into a perpendicular magnetic sector of flux density 0.450 T (into the page). What speed does the particle reach upon entering the magnetic field?
items.workedSolution: Equating ½mv² = |q|V_acc gives v = √(2|q|V_acc / m) = √(2 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ × 1200 / 1.16 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) = 1.82 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by 4 instead of 2 inside the square root.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes v² = 2|q|V_acc / m without taking the square root.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Forgets the ½ in ½mv² = |q|V_acc and computes √(|q|V_acc / m).

items.stem: An experimental parallel-plate laboratory condenser features plates of area 0.35 m² at initial spacing 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ m filled with a medium of relative permittivity 3.5 and charged to 350 V (take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). The plates are disconnected from the DC source so the plates remain electrically isolated, and the plate separation is then adjusted to 2.50 × 10⁻⁴ m while εᵣ stays at 3.5. What is the new potential difference across the isolated plates?
items.workedSolution: For isolated plates, charge Q is conserved while C′ = C₀(d/d′). Therefore V′ = Q / C′ = V₀(d′/d) = 350 × (0.00025 / 0.0005) = 175 V.

markScheme.criterion: Uses charge conservation V′ = V₀(d′/d) to obtain 175 V (D).

items.stem: A uniform 0.480 T magnetic field (directed out of the page) fills a medical radioisotope cyclotron chamber. Entering at right angles to the field with speed 4.50 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹, a single proton of charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg curves along a circular trajectory. If the particle completes a semicircular turn to strike a flat detector wall on the entry plane, how far from the entry slit does it hit?
items.workedSolution: Cyclotron radius r = mv / (|q|B) = 0.0979 m. Across a semicircular turn, the impact distance from the entry slit equals the orbit diameter D = 2r = 0.196 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds r = mv/(|q|B) and doubles to diameter D = 2r = 0.196 m (B).

items.stem: In an electron-microscope Wien monochromator, parallel plates separated by 0.02 m are held at 320 V (upper plate negative) perpendicular to a uniform 0.12 T magnetic field (out of the page). A proton (charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally to the right at 8.00 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. At what speed would a proton instead have to enter this same selector to pass straight through undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Electric field E = V / d = 320 / 0.02 = 1.60 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. Undeflected transmission requires qvB = qE, giving v_sel = E / B = 1.33 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In the inverter DC-link module shown between terminals A and B, capacitor C₁ = 200 μF is connected in series with the parallel pair C₂ = 40 μF and C₃ = 60 μF. Every capacitor has a maximum safe working voltage of 60 V. What is the maximum safe potential difference that can be applied across terminals A and B without exceeding the rating of any capacitor?
items.workedSolution: Parallel pair C_p = C₂ + C₃ = 100 μF. Because C₁ (200 μF) and C_p (100 μF) carry equal series charge Q, the smaller capacitance (parallel pair of capacitors) reaches 60 V first. Thus V_AB,max = 60 × (1 + 100 / 200) = 90.00 V ≈ 90.0 V.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies that the parallel pair of capacitors limits the voltage and calculates V_AB,max = 90.0 V.

items.stem: Within a bicycle hub-generator demonstrator, uniform magnetic flux of density 0.35 T links a rotor coil of 80 turns and area 0.01 m² rotating at 60 Hz from maximum flux linkage at t = 0 up to t = 0.00278 s. What is the peak emf ε₀ generated by the rotating coil?
items.workedSolution: Angular speed ω = 2πf = 2π(60) = 377 rad s⁻¹. Peak emf ε₀ = NBAω = 80 × 0.35 × 0.01 × 377 = 106 V.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the amplitude and reports peak-to-peak emf 2ε₀ instead of peak emf ε₀.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes single-turn peak emf BAω and omits multiplying by N turns.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes rotational frequency f directly into NBAω instead of angular speed ω = 2πf, omitting the 2π factor.

items.stem: In an electrostatic cathode-ray oscilloscope tube, an electron (charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) enters horizontally at 1.40 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹ along the midplane between parallel deflecting plates of length 0.04 m and separation 0.05 m maintained at 959 V (neglecting gravity). What is the magnitude of the transverse deflection as the particle exits the plates?
items.workedSolution: Transit time t = L / v₀ = 0.04 / 1.40 × 10⁷ = 2.86 × 10⁻⁹ s. Transverse acceleration a_y = |q|V / (md) = 3.37 × 10¹⁵ m s⁻². Deflection |Δy| = ½ a_y t² = 0.0137 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t = L/v₀, a_y = |q|V/(md), and |Δy| = ½a_y t² = 0.0137 m (C).

items.stem: During load testing on a laboratory slip-ring alternator with ohmic load, an ideal rotor coil (350 turns, area 0.025 m²) turns at 60 Hz in a uniform 0.3 T field while connected to a 20 Ω resistor. What mean electrical power is dissipated in the resistive load over a complete cycle?
items.workedSolution: Peak emf ε₀ = 2πfNBA = 990 V; V_rms = ε₀ / √2 = 700 V. Mean resistive power P_mean = V_rms² / R = ½ ε₀² / R = 2.45 × 10⁴ W.

markScheme.criterion: Computes ε₀ = 2πfNBA and mean power P_mean = ½ε₀²/R = 2.45 × 10⁴ W (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides peak power V₀I₀ by √2 instead of 2, forgetting that both V_rms = V₀/√2 and I_rms = I₀/√2 contribute a 1/√2 factor.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates peak instantaneous power V₀²/R without applying the ½ sinusoidal average factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides V₀ by 2 instead of √2 before squaring in V_rms²/R, introducing a ¼ factor.

items.stem: Ions of two chlorine isotopes carrying charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C (m₁ = 5.81 × 10⁻²⁶ kg, m₂ = 6.14 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) emerge from the E = 6.80 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹, B₁ = 0.25 T selector of a cosmochemistry meteorite isotope separator into a perpendicular B₂ = 0.6 T deflection chamber (into the page).

markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = m₁v / (qB₂) with chamber field B₂.
Doubles the radius difference ΔD = 2(r₂ − r₁).

parts.prompt: Calculate the common speed of the ions emerging from the velocity selector.
Determine the orbital radius r₁ of the lighter isotope in the deflection chamber.
Calculate the separation ΔD between the two isotope strike points on the detector wall.

items.stem: Perpendicular magnetic field lines through a closed earth-inductor compass loop (75 turns, area 0.022 m², resistance 2 Ω) change from +0.35 T to −0.350 T in 0.2 s. What total magnitude of electric charge ΔQ flows around the circuit during this reversal?
items.workedSolution: Signed field change |ΔB| = |-0.35 − 0.35| = 0.7 T, so |Δ(NΦ)| = 75 × 0.7 × 0.022 = 1.15 Wb. Induced charge ΔQ = |Δ(NΦ)| / R = 0.577 C.

markScheme.criterion: Accounts for field sign reversal in |Δ(NΦ)| and evaluates ΔQ = |Δ(NΦ)|/R = 0.577 C (A).

items.stem: Travelling to the left at constant velocity 8 m s⁻¹, a crossbar of resistance 0.4 Ω spans frictionless rails 0.2 m apart on a linear regenerator test track connected to a 1.4 Ω load in a 0.9 T field (directed out of the page). What induced current circulates around the closed loop?
items.workedSolution: Motional emf ε = BLv = 0.9 × 0.2 × 8 = 1.44 V. Loop current I = ε / (R + r) = 1.44 / 1.8 = 0.800 A.

items.stem: In the student switched RC bench rig shown, a capacitor of capacitance C = 200 μF is first fully charged to V₀ = 8.00 V by closing Switch A while Switches B and C remain open. Switch A is then opened and Switch B is closed so the capacitor discharges through R₁ = 90 kΩ for 12.0 s. At t = 12.0 s, while Switch B stays closed, Switch C is closed to connect R₂ = 45 kΩ in parallel with R₁ for a further 6.00 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) One farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates. (b)(i) τ₁ = R₁C = 18.00 s, so V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁) = 4.107 V ≈ 4.11 V (confirming 4.1 V). (b)(ii) R_eq = R₁R₂/(R₁+R₂) = 30.0 kΩ, giving τ₂ = R_eq C = 6.000 s ≈ 6.00 s. (b)(iii) V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂) = 1.511 V ≈ 1.51 V. (b)(iv) smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.

markScheme.criterion: Mentions charge stored per unit potential difference (coulombs per volt).
Complete SI unit definition: capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
Evaluates stage-1 time constant τ₁ = R₁C = 18.0 s.
Correctly substitutes V₀, t₁, and τ₁ into V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁).
Shows V₁ = 4.107 V (≥3 s.f.: 4.11 V), clearly matching 4.1 V.
Combines R₁ || R₂ = 30.0 kΩ and calculates τ₂ = R_eq C = 6.00 s.
Substitutes V₁ (accepting rounded prompt value on ECF), t₂, and τ₂ into V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂).
Correct final potential difference V₂ = 1.51 V.
States correctly that V₂ would be smaller (smaller/larger matching direction).
Explains via time constants in both stages: smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.

parts.prompt: Define the farad.
parts.expectedAnswer: The farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
workingSteps: Recall the unit definition linking electric charge in coulombs and potential difference in volts.

parts.prompt: Show clearly that after discharging through R₁ alone for 12.0 s, the potential difference across the capacitor is approximately 4.1 V.
parts.expectedAnswer: 4.107 V (which rounds to 4.11 V and 4.1 V)
workingSteps: Stage 1 time constant τ₁ = R₁ C = (90 × 10³ Ω) × (200 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 18.00 s.
Substitute into V₁ = V₀ exp(−t₁ / τ₁) = 8.000 V × exp(−12 / 18.00 s).
Evaluate to 4 s.f.: V₁ = 4.107 V ≈ 4.11 V (confirming approximately 4.1 V).

parts.prompt: At the instant Switch C closes, calculate the new time constant τ₂ of the discharge circuit.
workingSteps: Combined parallel resistance R_eq = (R₁ R₂)/(R₁ + R₂) = (90 × 45) / (90 + 45) = 30.0 kΩ.
New time constant τ₂ = R_eq C = (30 × 10³ Ω) × (200 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 6.000 s ≈ 6.00 s.

parts.prompt: Calculate the potential difference V₂ across the capacitor after a further 6.00 s with both Switch B and Switch C closed.
workingSteps: Start Stage 2 decay from V₁ = 4.107 V with time constant τ₂ = 6.000 s.

parts.prompt: Without calculation, state and explain how the final potential difference V₂ would change if resistor R₁ were replaced by a smaller resistor throughout the entire experiment.
parts.expectedAnswer: Replacing the first resistor with a smaller resistor gives a smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.
workingSteps: A smaller resistance changes both the initial discharge time constant and the combined parallel resistance in the same direction.
Link the altered time constants in both stages to the rate of exponential decay and the remaining potential difference.

items.stem: After disconnecting its charging cell in a pulsed laser pre-ioniser loop, capacitor C₁ = 20 μF at V₁ = 17 V shares charge across switch S with C₂ = 60 μF, which is initially uncharged. How much electrostatic energy is dissipated in the connecting leads as equilibrium is reached?
items.workedSolution: Initial energy U_i = 2.89 × 10⁻³ J. Final common voltage V_f = 4.25 V gives final energy U_f = ½(C₁ + C₂)V_f² = 7.22 × 10⁻⁴ J. Energy dissipated ΔU = U_i − U_f = 2.17 × 10⁻³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates U_i − U_f after conserving charge to obtain 2.17 × 10⁻³ J (D).

items.stem: Fixed so that a uniform magnetic field forms an angle of 25° with the plane of the coil, a closed search coil in an MRI fringe-field survey of 60 turns, area 0.016 m², and resistance 5 Ω experiences a field that decays uniformly from 0.56 T to zero in 0.1 s. What average induced current circulates around the closed coil during the ramp?
items.workedSolution: With θ_normal = 65°, |ε| = N|ΔB|A cos 65° / Δt = 2.27 V. Average current I = |ε| / R = 2.27 / 5 = 0.454 A.

markScheme.criterion: Computes |ε| using θ_normal = 65° and I = |ε|/R = 0.454 A (B).

items.stem: In a camera strobe flash bank, two initially uncharged capacitors of capacitances C₁ = 12 μF and C₂ = 24 μF are connected in series across a 11 V DC source. What is the total equivalent capacitance of the series pair?
items.workedSolution: For series capacitors, 1/C_eq = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂, giving C_eq = (12 × 24)/(12 + 24) μF = 8.00 × 10⁻⁶ F.

items.stem: The industrial snubber network shown between terminals A and B combines C₁ = 75 μF in series with the parallel pair C₂ = 120 μF and C₃ = 105 μF. Each individual capacitor is rated to a maximum safe working potential difference of 100 V.
items.workedSolution: (a) C_p = 225 μF, C_eq = 56.25 μF ≈ 56.3 μF. (b) The single series capacitor hits 100 V first, giving V_AB,max = 133.3 V ≈ 133 V. (c) E_max = ½ C_eq V_AB,max² = 0.5000 J ≈ 0.500 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies equal series charge Q and that the single series capacitor reaches 100 V first.

parts.prompt: Calculate the combined capacitance of the network between A and B in μF.
workingSteps: Parallel branch: C_p = C₂ + C₃ = 120 + 105 = 225 μF.
Series combination: C_eq = (C₁ C_p) / (C₁ + C_p) = (75 × 225) / (75 + 225) = 56.25 μF ≈ 56.3 μF.

parts.prompt: Determine the maximum safe potential difference that can be applied across A and B, stating which section reaches its voltage rating first.
parts.expectedAnswer: 133 V (limited by the single series capacitor)
workingSteps: In series both sections hold equal charge Q, so V ∝ 1/C; the smaller capacitance (single series capacitor) reaches 100 V first.
Maximum safe total pd V_AB,max = 100 × (1 + 75 / 225) = 133.3 V ≈ 133 V.

items.workedSolution: Secondary rms voltage V_s = V_p(N_s/N_p) = 120(40/800) = 6.00 V. Output power P_out = V_s² / R_L = 1.50 W. Input power P_in = P_out / η = 1.70 W, so I_p = P_in / V_p = 0.0142 A.

markScheme.criterion: Computes V_s, P_out, and I_p = P_out / (η V_p) = 0.0142 A (D).

items.stem: Selected at common speed by E = 4.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ and B₁ = 0.25 T in a paleoclimate ice-core Bainbridge analyser, chlorine ions of charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and masses m₁ = 5.81 × 10⁻²⁶ kg and m₂ = 6.14 × 10⁻²⁶ kg enter a uniform B₂ = 0.6 T chamber (into the page) and complete semicircular paths. What is the straight-line separation ΔD between the two isotope strike marks on the detector wall?
items.workedSolution: Selected speed v = E / B₁ = 1.60 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. Semicircular strike separation ΔD = 2(r₂ − r₁) = 2(m₂ − m₁)E / (q B₁ B₂) = 0.0110 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the difference in orbital radii |r₂ − r₁| and forgets the factor of 2 for semicircular impact diameters ΔD = 2|r₂ − r₁|.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses B₁² in the denominator instead of the product B₁B₂ of selector and chamber fields.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Reports the semicircular strike distance 2r₁ of the lighter isotope rather than the separation between isotopes.

items.stem: In the electronic shutter decay bank shown, a capacitor of capacitance C = 220 μF is first fully charged to V₀ = 11.0 V by closing Switch A while Switches B and C remain open. Switch A is then opened and Switch B is closed so the capacitor discharges through R₁ = 60 kΩ for 9.00 s. At t = 9.00 s, while Switch B stays closed, Switch C is closed to connect R₂ = 20 kΩ in parallel with R₁ for a further 4.00 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) One farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates. (b)(i) τ₁ = R₁C = 13.20 s, so V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁) = 5.563 V ≈ 5.56 V (confirming 5.6 V). (b)(ii) R_eq = R₁R₂/(R₁+R₂) = 15.0 kΩ, giving τ₂ = R_eq C = 3.300 s ≈ 3.30 s. (b)(iii) V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂) = 1.655 V ≈ 1.66 V. (b)(iv) smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.

markScheme.criterion: Mentions charge stored per unit potential difference (coulombs per volt).
Complete SI unit definition: capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
Evaluates stage-1 time constant τ₁ = R₁C = 13.2 s.
Correctly substitutes V₀, t₁, and τ₁ into V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁).
Shows V₁ = 5.563 V (≥3 s.f.: 5.56 V), clearly matching 5.6 V.
Combines R₁ || R₂ = 15.0 kΩ and calculates τ₂ = R_eq C = 3.30 s.
Substitutes V₁ (accepting rounded prompt value on ECF), t₂, and τ₂ into V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂).
Correct final potential difference V₂ = 1.66 V.
States correctly that V₂ would be smaller (smaller/larger matching direction).
Explains via time constants in both stages: smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.

parts.prompt: Define the farad.
parts.expectedAnswer: The farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
workingSteps: Recall the unit definition linking electric charge in coulombs and potential difference in volts.

parts.prompt: Show clearly that after discharging through R₁ alone for 9.00 s, the potential difference across the capacitor is approximately 5.6 V.
parts.expectedAnswer: 5.563 V (which rounds to 5.56 V and 5.6 V)
workingSteps: Stage 1 time constant τ₁ = R₁ C = (60 × 10³ Ω) × (220 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 13.20 s.
Substitute into V₁ = V₀ exp(−t₁ / τ₁) = 11.00 V × exp(−9 / 13.20 s).
Evaluate to 4 s.f.: V₁ = 5.563 V ≈ 5.56 V (confirming approximately 5.6 V).

parts.prompt: At the instant Switch C closes, calculate the new time constant τ₂ of the discharge circuit.
workingSteps: Combined parallel resistance R_eq = (R₁ R₂)/(R₁ + R₂) = (60 × 20) / (60 + 20) = 15.0 kΩ.
New time constant τ₂ = R_eq C = (15 × 10³ Ω) × (220 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 3.300 s ≈ 3.30 s.

parts.prompt: Calculate the potential difference V₂ across the capacitor after a further 4.00 s with both Switch B and Switch C closed.
workingSteps: Start Stage 2 decay from V₁ = 5.563 V with time constant τ₂ = 3.300 s.

parts.prompt: Without calculation, state and explain how the final potential difference V₂ would change if resistor R₁ were replaced by a smaller resistor throughout the entire experiment.
parts.expectedAnswer: Replacing the first resistor with a smaller resistor gives a smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.
workingSteps: A smaller resistance changes both the initial discharge time constant and the combined parallel resistance in the same direction.
Link the altered time constants in both stages to the rate of exponential decay and the remaining potential difference.

items.stem: During a charge-conservation test on a charge-redistribution DAC bench circuit, C₁ = 20 μF at initial voltage V₁ = 37 V is connected by closing switch S across C₂ = 80 μF (initially uncharged).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Q_net = C₁V₁ + C₂V₂ before switch closure.
Divides conserved charge from (a) by C₁ + C₂.
Subtracts final stored energy ½(C₁ + C₂)V_f² from initial stored energy.

items.stem: An experimental rotary position-sensing pickup winding comprises 300 closely wound turns of area 0.016 m² and resistance 5 Ω. Held at a fixed orientation where the field lines make an angle of 35° with the plane of the coil, the field ramps uniformly from 0.36 T to 1.08 T over 0.05 s.

Divides induced emf from (b) by coil resistance R.

items.stem: Emerging through the anode aperture after acceleration from rest across 3600 V in a surface-science low-energy ion scattering rig, a doubly ionised magnesium ion (+3.20 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 3.98 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) enters at 90° to a homogeneous 0.320 T magnetic field (out of the page). If the particle completes a semicircular turn onto an exit detector plate, what is the strike diameter D from the entry slit?
items.workedSolution: Speed v = √(2|q|V_acc / m) = 2.41 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹; radius r = mv / (|q|B) = 0.0935 m. Semicircular detector separation D = 2r = 0.187 m.

items.stem: A piezo-positioned capacitor stage has plate area 0.25 m², initial separation 4.00 × 10⁻⁴ m, and relative permittivity 4, energised initially at 100 V (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). Next, the assembly is kept connected across the DC source at constant potential difference while the plate separation is adjusted to 0.001 m with εᵣ = 4 throughout. What is the final electrostatic energy stored in the modified state?
items.workedSolution: Initial capacitance C = 2.21 × 10⁻⁸ F, modified capacitance C′ = 8.85 × 10⁻⁹ F. Under constant-voltage, final stored energy U′ = 4.42 × 10⁻⁵ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes modified capacitance C′ and evaluates final stored energy 4.42 × 10⁻⁵ J (D).

items.stem: In a biomedical amplifier coupling network, parallel branches containing C_p1 = 10 μF and C_p2 = 20 μF are wired in series with capacitor C_s = 30 μF and charged by a steady 7 V source.

markScheme.criterion: Sums C_p = C_p1 + C_p2 and combines in series with C_s.
Finds total charge Q = C_eq V₀ and divides by C_p.

workingSteps: C_p = C_p1 + C_p2; C_eq = (C_s C_p)/(C_s + C_p).

items.stem: Inside a fine-beam Helmholtz tube, an electron (charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) enters at 8.00 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ perpendicular to a uniform 2.40 × 10⁻³ T magnetic field directed into the page and follows a circular arc. What is the radius of curvature r of the circular path?
items.workedSolution: Equating magnetic and centripetal forces |q|vB = mv²/r gives r = mv / (|q|B) = (9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg × 8.00 × 10⁶) / (0 × 2.40 × 10⁻³) = 0.0190 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the cyclotron radius formula and evaluates |q|B / (mv) instead of mv / (|q|B).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Confuses orbital radius r = mv/(|q|B) with semicircular orbit diameter D = 2r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses mv²/(|q|B) by forgetting to cancel one power of speed v when equating mv²/r = |q|vB.

items.stem: During tuning of an accelerator-mass-spectrometry pre-filter (180 V across a 0.03 m gap, upper plate positive, with B = 0.32 T into the page), a proton of charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg is injected horizontally along the central axis. At what speed must the proton travel to pass straight through the exit slit undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Uniform electric field E = V / d = 180 / 0.03 = 6.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹. Zero net deflection requires qE = qvB, so v_sel = E / B = V / (Bd) = 1.88 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_sel = V / (Bd) to obtain 1.88 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: In the power-supply smoothing stage shown between terminals A and B, capacitor C₁ = 60 μF is connected in series with the parallel pair C₂ = 80 μF and C₃ = 40 μF. Every capacitor has a maximum safe working voltage of 50 V. What is the maximum safe potential difference that can be applied across terminals A and B without exceeding the rating of any capacitor?
items.workedSolution: Parallel pair C_p = C₂ + C₃ = 120 μF. Because C₁ (60 μF) and C_p (120 μF) carry equal series charge Q, the smaller capacitance (single series capacitor) reaches 50 V first. Thus V_AB,max = 50 × (1 + 60 / 120) = 75.00 V ≈ 75.0 V.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies that the single series capacitor limits the voltage and calculates V_AB,max = 75.0 V.

items.stem: Within an industrial watchdog reset timer, a 24 V DC rail charges an initially uncharged 25 μF capacitor via a 2.5 kΩ series resistor; the transient is evaluated at 0.138 s.

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies resistance in Ω by capacitance in F (τ = RC).
Uses U = ½CV_C² with the voltage found in (b).

parts.prompt: Calculate the RC time constant τ of the circuit.
Determine the potential difference across the capacitor at t = 0.138 s.
Calculate the electrostatic energy stored in the capacitor at t = 0.138 s.

items.stem: Driven at a rotational frequency of 40 Hz inside a wind-tunnel slip-ring test dynamo, a slip-ring coil of 50 turns and area 0.03 m² cuts a uniform 0.14 T magnetic field (starting from maximum flux at t = 0 and observed at t = 0.00208 s). What is the peak-to-peak emf displayed on an oscilloscope across one full cycle?
items.workedSolution: Peak emf ε₀ = 2πfNBA = 52.8 V. Peak-to-peak emf V_pp = 2ε₀ = 106 V.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes rms voltage ε₀/√2 instead of peak-to-peak voltage 2ε₀.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by 2 for peak-to-peak but omits 2π when converting f to ω.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Reports single-sided peak amplitude ε₀ rather than peak-to-peak swing 2ε₀.

items.stem: Travelling at an initial horizontal speed of 5.00 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹, a proton (q = +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) passes centrally between parallel plates of length 0.05 m spaced 0.04 m apart across a 1140 V potential difference in an inkjet micro-droplet deflection stage. What is the angular deflection θ (in degrees) of the particle velocity as it leaves the plates?
items.workedSolution: |v_y| = a_y t = (|q|V / md)(L / v₀) = 2.73 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. Therefore θ = arctan(|v_y| / v₀) = 28.6°.

Determine the useful electrical power delivered to the secondary load.

items.stem: A micro-grid synchronous generator bench uses a coil of negligible internal resistance with 180 turns and area 0.025 m² spinning at 25 Hz in a uniform 0.22 T magnetic field across a 16 Ω resistor. What root-mean-square (rms) current flows through the load resistor?
items.workedSolution: ε₀ = 2πfNBA = 156 V, so V_rms = ε₀ / √2 = 110 V. Load rms current I_rms = V_rms / R = 110 / 16 = 6.87 A.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 2π factor when converting frequency f into angular speed ω = 2πf.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates peak current I₀ = ε₀/R and omits dividing by √2 for rms current.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides peak current I₀ by 2 instead of √2.

items.stem: Operating with selector electric field 6.80 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹, selector flux density 0.35 T, and chamber flux density 0.7 T (out of the page), a planetary-probe isotopic magnetic sector separates carbon ions of charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and masses 1.99 × 10⁻²⁶ kg and 2.32 × 10⁻²⁶ kg onto a flat detector plane.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = m₁v / (qB₂) with chamber field B₂.
Doubles the radius difference ΔD = 2(r₂ − r₁).

parts.prompt: Calculate the common speed of the ions emerging from the velocity selector.
Determine the orbital radius r₁ of the lighter isotope in the deflection chamber.
Calculate the separation ΔD between the two isotope strike points on the detector wall.

items.stem: Perpendicular magnetic field lines through a closed electromagnet pole-gap calibration search coil (50 turns, area 0.01 m², resistance 12 Ω) change from +0.48 T to −0.288 T in 0.08 s. What is the magnitude of the average emf induced in the coil during the reversal?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates |ΔB| across sign reversal to obtain |ε| = 4.80 V (A).

options.distractorRationale: Treats the field as dropping only to zero (ΔB = B₁) rather than reversing sign to B₂.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the field magnitudes |B₁| − |B₂| instead of taking the signed vector difference |B₂ − B₁|.

options.distractorRationale: Divides emf by resistance R, reporting induced current instead of induced emf.

items.stem: In an electromagnetic rail-braking demonstrator, parallel rails of separation 0.5 m are closed by a 4.2 Ω resistor inside a perpendicular 0.45 T magnetic field (directed into the page). A metal rod of resistance 1.2 Ω moves steadily to the right at 4 m s⁻¹. What mechanical power must be supplied to keep the rod moving at constant speed?
items.workedSolution: ε = BLv = 0.900 V; R_tot = 4.2 + 1.2 = 5.4 Ω. Mechanical input power equals total Joule heating P = ε² / R_tot = 0.150 W.

items.stem: In the two-stage pulse-shaping circuit shown, a capacitor of capacitance C = 250 μF is first fully charged to V₀ = 9.00 V by closing Switch A while Switches B and C remain open. Switch A is then opened and Switch B is closed so the capacitor discharges through R₁ = 60 kΩ for 10.0 s. At t = 10.0 s, while Switch B stays closed, Switch C is closed to connect R₂ = 30 kΩ in parallel with R₁ for a further 6.00 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) One farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates. (b)(i) τ₁ = R₁C = 15.00 s, so V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁) = 4.621 V ≈ 4.62 V (confirming 4.6 V). (b)(ii) R_eq = R₁R₂/(R₁+R₂) = 20.0 kΩ, giving τ₂ = R_eq C = 5.000 s ≈ 5.00 s. (b)(iii) V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂) = 1.392 V ≈ 1.39 V. (b)(iv) larger final potential difference because the time constant increases and the capacitor discharges more slowly.

markScheme.criterion: Mentions charge stored per unit potential difference (coulombs per volt).
Complete SI unit definition: capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
Evaluates stage-1 time constant τ₁ = R₁C = 15.0 s.
Correctly substitutes V₀, t₁, and τ₁ into V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁).
Shows V₁ = 4.621 V (≥3 s.f.: 4.62 V), clearly matching 4.6 V.
Combines R₁ || R₂ = 20.0 kΩ and calculates τ₂ = R_eq C = 5.00 s.
Substitutes V₁ (accepting rounded prompt value on ECF), t₂, and τ₂ into V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂).
Correct final potential difference V₂ = 1.39 V.
States correctly that V₂ would be larger (smaller/larger matching direction).
Explains via time constants in both stages: larger final potential difference because the time constant increases and the capacitor discharges more slowly.

parts.prompt: Define the farad.
parts.expectedAnswer: The farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
workingSteps: Recall the unit definition linking electric charge in coulombs and potential difference in volts.

parts.prompt: Show clearly that after discharging through R₁ alone for 10.0 s, the potential difference across the capacitor is approximately 4.6 V.
parts.expectedAnswer: 4.621 V (which rounds to 4.62 V and 4.6 V)
workingSteps: Stage 1 time constant τ₁ = R₁ C = (60 × 10³ Ω) × (250 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 15.00 s.
Substitute into V₁ = V₀ exp(−t₁ / τ₁) = 9.000 V × exp(−10 / 15.00 s).
Evaluate to 4 s.f.: V₁ = 4.621 V ≈ 4.62 V (confirming approximately 4.6 V).

parts.prompt: At the instant Switch C closes, calculate the new time constant τ₂ of the discharge circuit.
workingSteps: Combined parallel resistance R_eq = (R₁ R₂)/(R₁ + R₂) = (60 × 30) / (60 + 30) = 20.0 kΩ.
New time constant τ₂ = R_eq C = (20 × 10³ Ω) × (250 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 5.000 s ≈ 5.00 s.

parts.prompt: Calculate the potential difference V₂ across the capacitor after a further 6.00 s with both Switch B and Switch C closed.
workingSteps: Start Stage 2 decay from V₁ = 4.621 V with time constant τ₂ = 5.000 s.

parts.prompt: Without calculation, state and explain how the final potential difference V₂ would change if resistor R₁ were replaced by a larger resistor throughout the entire experiment.
parts.expectedAnswer: Replacing the first resistor with a larger resistor gives a larger final potential difference because the time constant increases and the capacitor discharges more slowly.
workingSteps: A larger resistance changes both the initial discharge time constant and the combined parallel resistance in the same direction.
Link the altered time constants in both stages to the rate of exponential decay and the remaining potential difference.

items.stem: In a telemetry energy-transfer buffer, capacitor C₁ = 25 μF is charged to V₁ = 41 V, isolated from its supply, and then connected via switch S in parallel with capacitor C₂ = 75 μF (initially uncharged). What final common potential difference is established across both capacitors?
items.workedSolution: Total conserved charge Q_net = C₁V₁ + C₂V₂ = 1.02 × 10⁻³ C. Final parallel capacitance C_eq = 100 μF, so V_f = Q_net / (C₁ + C₂) = 10.3 V.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves net charge Q_net and divides by C₁ + C₂ to obtain 10.3 V (C).

items.stem: A non-destructive eddy-current probe winding has 200 turns, cross-sectional area 0.008 m², and total loop resistance 5 Ω. Uniform magnetic field lines make an angle of 60° with the plane of the coil while the flux density ramps uniformly from 0.22 T to 0.55 T over 0.025 s. What is the initial magnetic flux linkage NΦ₁ of the coil?
items.workedSolution: Angle to coil normal θ_n = 30°. Initial flux linkage NΦ₁ = NBA cos θ_n = 200 × 0.22 × 0.008 × cos 30° = 0.305 Wb.

markScheme.criterion: Uses θ_normal = 30° in NΦ₁ = NBA cos θ_normal to obtain 0.305 Wb (C).

items.stem: An uncharged network in a precision timing reference board connects C_s = 24 μF in series with two parallel capacitors C_p1 = 16 μF and C_p2 = 32 μF across an ideal 13 V cell. What total electrostatic energy is stored in the complete network?
items.workedSolution: Parallel bank C_p = 48 μF; total C_eq = 1.60 × 10⁻⁵ F. Stored energy U = ½C_eq V₀² = 0.5 × 1.60 × 10⁻⁵ × (13)² = 1.35 × 10⁻³ J.

parts.prompt: Calculate the combined capacitance of the network between A and B in μF.
workingSteps: Parallel branch: C_p = C₂ + C₃ = 100 + 60 = 160 μF.
Series combination: C_eq = (C₁ C_p) / (C₁ + C_p) = (80 × 160) / (80 + 160) = 53.33 μF ≈ 53.3 μF.

parts.prompt: Determine the maximum safe potential difference that can be applied across A and B, stating which section reaches its voltage rating first.
parts.expectedAnswer: 75.0 V (limited by the single series capacitor)
workingSteps: In series both sections hold equal charge Q, so V ∝ 1/C; the smaller capacitance (single series capacitor) reaches 50 V first.
Maximum safe total pd V_AB,max = 50 × (1 + 80 / 160) = 75.00 V ≈ 75.0 V.

parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum electrical energy safely stored in the complete network.

items.stem: When switch S closes in an industrial watchdog reset timer, a 25 μF uncharged capacitor charges from a 9 V cell through a 10 kΩ resistor over an interval of 0.375 s. How much electrostatic energy is stored in the capacitor at t = 0.375 s?
items.workedSolution: τ = RC = 0.250 s, giving V_C(0.375 s) = 6.99 V. Stored energy U = ½CV_C² = 0.5 × 2.50 × 10⁻⁵ × (6.99)² = 6.11 × 10⁻⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V_C(t) and computes U(t) = ½CV_C(t)² = 6.11 × 10⁻⁴ J (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates maximum stored energy ½CV₀² rather than the instantaneous energy at the query time.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Forgets the factor of one-half in U(t) = ½CV_C(t)².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Scales stored energy linearly with V_C(t)/V₀ instead of quadratically with (V_C(t)/V₀)² in U = ½CV_C².

items.stem: An aircraft auxiliary AC bus resistive test rig uses a coil of negligible internal resistance with 280 turns and area 0.012 m² spinning at 25 Hz in a uniform 0.22 T magnetic field across a 40 Ω resistor.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P_mean = I_rms² R (= ½ ε₀ I₀).

parts.prompt: Calculate the peak emf ε₀ induced in the rotating coil.
Determine the rms current in the resistive load.
Calculate the mean electrical power dissipated in the load.

items.stem: A planetary-probe isotopic magnetic sector filters potassium ions (charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, masses m₁ = 6.47 × 10⁻²⁶ kg and m₂ = 6.81 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) using crossed fields E = 9.60 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ and B₁ = 0.25 T, then bends them through semicircular arcs onto a detector plate in a chamber field B₂ = 0.6 T (into the page). How far from the entry slit S does the lighter isotope strike the detector wall?
items.workedSolution: v = E / B₁ = 3.84 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ and r₁ = m₁v / (qB₂) = 0.259 m. Strike distance from slit S is D₁ = 2r₁ = 0.518 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reports the orbital radius r₁ rather than the semicircular chord distance D₁ = 2r₁ from slit S.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses B₁² instead of B₁B₂ in D₁ = 2m₁E/(qB₁B₂).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the separation ΔD between the two isotopes rather than the slit-to-impact distance 2r₁.

items.stem: Perpendicular magnetic field lines through a closed cryogenic solenoid quench-sensing coil (350 turns, area 0.022 m², resistance 2 Ω) change from +0.8 T to −0.480 T in 0.2 s.

markScheme.criterion: Includes negative sign of reversed field in N(B₂ − B₁)A.

Determine the magnitude of the average induced emf.
Calculate the total magnitude of charge ΔQ that circulates through the coil.

items.stem: On a frictionless laboratory induction sled, a conducting bar of internal resistance 1.2 Ω slides to the left at a steady speed of 4 m s⁻¹ along parallel horizontal rails of negligible resistance spaced 0.2 m apart. A uniform 0.25 T magnetic field (directed into the page) threads the rails, which are bridged by a 1.4 Ω load resistor.

markScheme.criterion: Divides ε from (a) by total loop resistance R + r.
Equates applied force to magnetic braking force F = BIL.

items.stem: In the dual-rate relay delay circuit shown, a capacitor of capacitance C = 600 μF is first fully charged to V₀ = 14.0 V by closing Switch A while Switches B and C remain open. Switch A is then opened and Switch B is closed so the capacitor discharges through R₁ = 30 kΩ for 12.0 s. At t = 12.0 s, while Switch B stays closed, Switch C is closed to connect R₂ = 15 kΩ in parallel with R₁ for a further 5.00 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) One farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates. (b)(i) τ₁ = R₁C = 18.00 s, so V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁) = 7.188 V ≈ 7.19 V (confirming 7.2 V). (b)(ii) R_eq = R₁R₂/(R₁+R₂) = 10.0 kΩ, giving τ₂ = R_eq C = 6.000 s ≈ 6.00 s. (b)(iii) V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂) = 3.124 V ≈ 3.12 V. (b)(iv) larger final potential difference because the time constant increases and the capacitor discharges more slowly.

markScheme.criterion: Mentions charge stored per unit potential difference (coulombs per volt).
Complete SI unit definition: capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
Evaluates stage-1 time constant τ₁ = R₁C = 18.0 s.
Correctly substitutes V₀, t₁, and τ₁ into V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁).
Shows V₁ = 7.188 V (≥3 s.f.: 7.19 V), clearly matching 7.2 V.
Combines R₁ || R₂ = 10.0 kΩ and calculates τ₂ = R_eq C = 6.00 s.
Substitutes V₁ (accepting rounded prompt value on ECF), t₂, and τ₂ into V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂).
Correct final potential difference V₂ = 3.12 V.
States correctly that V₂ would be larger (smaller/larger matching direction).
Explains via time constants in both stages: larger final potential difference because the time constant increases and the capacitor discharges more slowly.

parts.prompt: Define the farad.
parts.expectedAnswer: The farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
workingSteps: Recall the unit definition linking electric charge in coulombs and potential difference in volts.

parts.prompt: Show clearly that after discharging through R₁ alone for 12.0 s, the potential difference across the capacitor is approximately 7.2 V.
parts.expectedAnswer: 7.188 V (which rounds to 7.19 V and 7.2 V)
workingSteps: Stage 1 time constant τ₁ = R₁ C = (30 × 10³ Ω) × (600 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 18.00 s.
Substitute into V₁ = V₀ exp(−t₁ / τ₁) = 14.00 V × exp(−12 / 18.00 s).
Evaluate to 4 s.f.: V₁ = 7.188 V ≈ 7.19 V (confirming approximately 7.2 V).

parts.prompt: At the instant Switch C closes, calculate the new time constant τ₂ of the discharge circuit.
workingSteps: Combined parallel resistance R_eq = (R₁ R₂)/(R₁ + R₂) = (30 × 15) / (30 + 15) = 10.0 kΩ.
New time constant τ₂ = R_eq C = (10 × 10³ Ω) × (600 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 6.000 s ≈ 6.00 s.

parts.prompt: Calculate the potential difference V₂ across the capacitor after a further 5.00 s with both Switch B and Switch C closed.
workingSteps: Start Stage 2 decay from V₁ = 7.188 V with time constant τ₂ = 6.000 s.

parts.prompt: Without calculation, state and explain how the final potential difference V₂ would change if resistor R₁ were replaced by a larger resistor throughout the entire experiment.
parts.expectedAnswer: Replacing the first resistor with a larger resistor gives a larger final potential difference because the time constant increases and the capacitor discharges more slowly.
workingSteps: A larger resistance changes both the initial discharge time constant and the combined parallel resistance in the same direction.
Link the altered time constants in both stages to the rate of exponential decay and the remaining potential difference.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Q_net = C₁V₁ + C₂V₂ before switch closure.
Divides conserved charge from (a) by C₁ + C₂.
Subtracts final stored energy ½(C₁ + C₂)V_f² from initial stored energy.

items.stem: During a dielectric bench test, a silicone elastomer sheet with relative permittivity 3.2 completely fills the 3.00 × 10⁻⁴ m gap between parallel metal plates of area 1.5 m² inside an industrial proximity-sensing pad. When the assembly is charged to 320 V (take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹), calculate the energy stored per unit volume inside the dielectric.
items.workedSolution: Uniform field E = V / d = 320 / 0.0003 = 1.07 × 10⁶ V m⁻¹. Energy density u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² = 0.5 × 3.2 × 8.85 × 10⁻¹² × (1.07 × 10⁶)² = 16.1 J m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = V/d and u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² to obtain 16.1 J m⁻³ (B).

items.stem: An experimental capacitive MEMS accelerometer features plates of area 0.7 m² at initial spacing 6.00 × 10⁻⁴ m filled with a medium of relative permittivity 6.5 and charged to 420 V (take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). The plates are disconnected from the DC source so the plates remain electrically isolated, and the plate separation is then adjusted to 3.00 × 10⁻⁴ m while εᵣ stays at 6.5. What is the new potential difference across the isolated plates?
items.workedSolution: For isolated plates, charge Q is conserved while C′ = C₀(d/d′). Therefore V′ = Q / C′ = V₀(d′/d) = 420 × (0.0003 / 0.0006) = 210 V.

markScheme.criterion: Uses charge conservation V′ = V₀(d′/d) to obtain 210 V (B).

Determine the potential difference across capacitor C₁.

items.stem: Injected orthogonally at 2.20 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ into the 0.220 T magnetic field (directed into the page) of a bubble-chamber momentum analyser, an alpha particle (q = +3.20 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 6.64 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) undergoes uniform circular motion in vacuum. What is the cyclotron revolution frequency f of the particle in this magnetic field?

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the formula and evaluates orbital period 2πm / (|q|B) instead of frequency.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes angular speed ω = |q|B / m and omits dividing by 2π for frequency f = ω / (2π).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides ω by π instead of 2π when converting angular speed to frequency.

items.stem: Within a vacuum accelerator monochromatic ion collimator, a proton (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally to the right at 1.50 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ between plates 0.015 m apart at p.d. 750 V (upper plate negative) inside a perpendicular 0.2 T field (out of the page). What is the initial upward transverse acceleration of the proton upon entering the crossed fields?
items.workedSolution: E = V/d = 5.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. Upward electric force F_E = qE = 8.00 × 10⁻¹⁵ N; downward magnetic force |F_B| = qvB = 4.80 × 10⁻¹⁵ N. Net upward acceleration a_y = (F_E − |F_B|) / m = 1.92 × 10¹² m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing qvB from qE and divides by m to obtain 1.92 × 10¹² m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: In the audio crossover filter shown between terminals A and B, capacitor C₁ = 40 μF is connected in series with the parallel pair C₂ = 70 μF and C₃ = 50 μF. Every capacitor has a maximum safe working voltage of 60 V. What is the maximum safe potential difference that can be applied across terminals A and B without exceeding the rating of any capacitor?
items.workedSolution: Parallel pair C_p = C₂ + C₃ = 120 μF. Because C₁ (40 μF) and C_p (120 μF) carry equal series charge Q, the smaller capacitance (single series capacitor) reaches 60 V first. Thus V_AB,max = 60 × (1 + 40 / 120) = 80.00 V ≈ 80.0 V.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies that the single series capacitor limits the voltage and calculates V_AB,max = 80.0 V.

items.stem: A 80 μF capacitor at 6 V in a sensor low-pass RC network discharges exponentially through a series resistance of 5 kΩ; measurements are recorded 0.16 s after closing the switch.

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies resistance in Ω by capacitance in F (τ = RC).
Uses U = ½CV_C² with the voltage found in (b).

parts.prompt: Calculate the RC time constant τ of the circuit.
Determine the potential difference across the capacitor at t = 0.16 s.
Calculate the electrostatic energy stored in the capacitor at t = 0.16 s.

items.stem: An armature of 400 turns and area 0.018 m² in a hydroelectric micro-turbine alternator spins at frequency 20 Hz within a uniform 0.35 T field; its coil normal is aligned with the field at t = 0, and an oscilloscope reads the output at t = 0.00833 s. What instantaneous emf ε is induced at t = 0.00833 s?
items.workedSolution: ω = 2π(20) = 126 rad s⁻¹, ε₀ = NBAω = 317 V. At t = 0.00833 s, ε(t) = ε₀ sin(ωt) = 274 V.

markScheme.criterion: Computes ε₀ = 2πfNBA and evaluates ε₀ sin(ωt) = 274 V (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reports the maximum amplitude ε₀ rather than evaluating ε(t) = ε₀ sin(ωt) at the specified instant.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits 2π when computing peak amplitude NBAω before multiplying by sin(ωt).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates ε₀ cos(ωt) instead of ε₀ sin(ωt), confusing the phase of induced emf with magnetic flux linkage.

items.stem: Inside the vacuum chamber of an inkjet micro-droplet deflection stage, electrodes 0.04 m long and 0.05 m apart are biased at 1820 V while an electron (q = −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) enters centrally at 1.60 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. What is the magnitude of the transverse deflection as the particle exits the plates?
items.workedSolution: Transit time t = L / v₀ = 0.04 / 1.60 × 10⁷ = 2.50 × 10⁻⁹ s. Transverse acceleration a_y = |q|V / (md) = 6.39 × 10¹⁵ m s⁻². Deflection |Δy| = ½ a_y t² = 0.0200 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t = L/v₀, a_y = |q|V/(md), and |Δy| = ½a_y t² = 0.0200 m (B).

items.stem: Across a pure 40 Ω load in a standby hospital alternator feeding a resistive heater, a coil of 280 turns and area 0.012 m² (negligible coil resistance) rotates uniformly at 40 Hz inside a 0.38 T magnetic field. What mean electrical power is dissipated in the resistive load over a complete cycle?
items.workedSolution: Peak emf ε₀ = 2πfNBA = 321 V; V_rms = ε₀ / √2 = 227 V. Mean resistive power P_mean = V_rms² / R = ½ ε₀² / R = 1.29 × 10³ W.

markScheme.criterion: Computes ε₀ = 2πfNBA and mean power P_mean = ½ε₀²/R = 1.29 × 10³ W (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides V₀ by 2 instead of √2 before squaring in V_rms²/R, introducing a ¼ factor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates peak instantaneous power V₀²/R without applying the ½ sinusoidal average factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides peak power V₀I₀ by √2 instead of 2, forgetting that both V_rms = V₀/√2 and I_rms = I₀/√2 contribute a 1/√2 factor.

items.stem: An ion beam containing potassium isotopes of masses 6.47 × 10⁻²⁶ kg and 6.81 × 10⁻²⁶ kg (common charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) is velocity-matched by E = 4.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ and B₁ = 0.25 T in a nuclear-forensics Bainbridge analyser before semicircular mass separation in B₂ = 0.6 T (into the page).

markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = m₁v / (qB₂) with chamber field B₂.
Doubles the radius difference ΔD = 2(r₂ − r₁).

parts.prompt: Calculate the common speed of the ions emerging from the velocity selector.
Determine the orbital radius r₁ of the lighter isotope in the deflection chamber.
Calculate the separation ΔD between the two isotope strike points on the detector wall.

items.stem: Connected to a charge integrator of total loop resistance 2 Ω, a flat earth-inductor compass loop containing 140 turns of area 0.022 m² faces normal to a field that reverses from +0.12 T to −0.120 T in 0.2 s. What total magnitude of electric charge ΔQ flows around the circuit during this reversal?
items.workedSolution: Signed field change |ΔB| = |-0.12 − 0.12| = 0.24 T, so |Δ(NΦ)| = 140 × 0.24 × 0.022 = 0.739 Wb. Induced charge ΔQ = |Δ(NΦ)| / R = 0.370 C.

markScheme.criterion: Accounts for field sign reversal in |Δ(NΦ)| and evaluates ΔQ = |Δ(NΦ)|/R = 0.370 C (A).

items.stem: A uniform 0.6 T magnetic field directed out of the page permeates a linear regenerator test track whose smooth conducting rails sit 0.32 m apart across a 2.4 Ω external resistor. An external agent pulls a rod of resistance 0.6 Ω to the right at constant speed 8 m s⁻¹. What is the terminal potential difference across the external load resistor?
items.workedSolution: ε = BLv = 1.54 V; loop current I = ε / (R + r) = 0.512 A. Terminal p.d. across load V_term = I R = 0.512 × 2.4 = 1.23 V.

markScheme.criterion: Uses V_term = BLv × R/(R + r) to obtain 1.23 V (A).

items.stem: In the industrial bleed-down controller shown, a capacitor of capacitance C = 500 μF is first fully charged to V₀ = 15.0 V by closing Switch A while Switches B and C remain open. Switch A is then opened and Switch B is closed so the capacitor discharges through R₁ = 40 kΩ for 14.0 s. At t = 14.0 s, while Switch B stays closed, Switch C is closed to connect R₂ = 40 kΩ in parallel with R₁ for a further 8.00 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) One farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates. (b)(i) τ₁ = R₁C = 20.00 s, so V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁) = 7.449 V ≈ 7.45 V (confirming 7.4 V). (b)(ii) R_eq = R₁R₂/(R₁+R₂) = 20.0 kΩ, giving τ₂ = R_eq C = 10.00 s ≈ 10.0 s. (b)(iii) V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂) = 3.347 V ≈ 3.35 V. (b)(iv) smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.

markScheme.criterion: Mentions charge stored per unit potential difference (coulombs per volt).
Complete SI unit definition: capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
Evaluates stage-1 time constant τ₁ = R₁C = 20.0 s.
Correctly substitutes V₀, t₁, and τ₁ into V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁).
Shows V₁ = 7.449 V (≥3 s.f.: 7.45 V), clearly matching 7.4 V.
Combines R₁ || R₂ = 20.0 kΩ and calculates τ₂ = R_eq C = 10.0 s.
Substitutes V₁ (accepting rounded prompt value on ECF), t₂, and τ₂ into V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂).
Correct final potential difference V₂ = 3.35 V.
States correctly that V₂ would be smaller (smaller/larger matching direction).
Explains via time constants in both stages: smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.

parts.prompt: Define the farad.
parts.expectedAnswer: The farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
workingSteps: Recall the unit definition linking electric charge in coulombs and potential difference in volts.

parts.prompt: Show clearly that after discharging through R₁ alone for 14.0 s, the potential difference across the capacitor is approximately 7.4 V.
parts.expectedAnswer: 7.449 V (which rounds to 7.45 V and 7.4 V)
workingSteps: Stage 1 time constant τ₁ = R₁ C = (40 × 10³ Ω) × (500 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 20.00 s.
Substitute into V₁ = V₀ exp(−t₁ / τ₁) = 15.00 V × exp(−14 / 20.00 s).
Evaluate to 4 s.f.: V₁ = 7.449 V ≈ 7.45 V (confirming approximately 7.4 V).

parts.prompt: At the instant Switch C closes, calculate the new time constant τ₂ of the discharge circuit.
workingSteps: Combined parallel resistance R_eq = (R₁ R₂)/(R₁ + R₂) = (40 × 40) / (40 + 40) = 20.0 kΩ.
New time constant τ₂ = R_eq C = (20 × 10³ Ω) × (500 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 10.00 s ≈ 10.0 s.

parts.prompt: Calculate the potential difference V₂ across the capacitor after a further 8.00 s with both Switch B and Switch C closed.
workingSteps: Start Stage 2 decay from V₁ = 7.449 V with time constant τ₂ = 10.00 s.

parts.prompt: Without calculation, state and explain how the final potential difference V₂ would change if resistor R₁ were replaced by a smaller resistor throughout the entire experiment.
parts.expectedAnswer: Replacing the first resistor with a smaller resistor gives a smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.
workingSteps: A smaller resistance changes both the initial discharge time constant and the combined parallel resistance in the same direction.
Link the altered time constants in both stages to the rate of exponential decay and the remaining potential difference.

items.stem: Switch S in a high-impedance electrometer calibration rig connects a pre-charged capacitor C₁ = 12 μF (V₁ = 29 V) in parallel with C₂ = 36 μF (charged separately to V₂ = 7 V and connected with like polarity), allowing equilibrium to be reached. What total electrostatic energy remains stored in the pair after equilibrium is reached?
items.workedSolution: Conserved charge Q_net = 6.00 × 10⁻⁴ C across C₁ + C₂ = 48 μF yields V_f = 12.5 V. Final stored energy U_f = ½(C₁ + C₂)V_f² = 3.75 × 10⁻³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds V_f from conserved charge and computes U_f = ½(C₁ + C₂)V_f² = 3.75 × 10⁻³ J (C).

items.stem: Maintaining an angle of 30° with the normal to the coil, the magnetic field threading a laboratory Helmholtz-coil pickup loop with 150 turns and area 0.025 m² (total resistance 16 Ω) decays uniformly from 0.56 T to zero in 0.1 s. What average induced current circulates around the closed coil during the ramp?
items.workedSolution: With θ_normal = 30°, |ε| = N|ΔB|A cos 30° / Δt = 18.2 V. Average current I = |ε| / R = 18.2 / 16 = 1.14 A.

markScheme.criterion: Computes |ε| using θ_normal = 30° and I = |ε|/R = 1.14 A (D).

parts.prompt: Calculate the combined capacitance of the network between A and B in μF.
workingSteps: Parallel branch: C_p = C₂ + C₃ = 85 + 50 = 135 μF.
Series combination: C_eq = (C₁ C_p) / (C₁ + C_p) = (45 × 135) / (45 + 135) = 33.75 μF ≈ 33.8 μF.

parts.prompt: Determine the maximum safe potential difference that can be applied across A and B, stating which section reaches its voltage rating first.
parts.expectedAnswer: 80.0 V (limited by the single series capacitor)
workingSteps: In series both sections hold equal charge Q, so V ∝ 1/C; the smaller capacitance (single series capacitor) reaches 60 V first.
Maximum safe total pd V_AB,max = 60 × (1 + 45 / 135) = 80.00 V ≈ 80.0 V.

items.stem: A 120 μF capacitor at 30 V in an oscilloscope RC time-constant practical discharges exponentially through a series resistance of 5 kΩ; measurements are recorded 0.72 s after closing the switch. What is the current in the resistor at t = 0.72 s?
items.workedSolution: Initial current I₀ = V₀ / R = 30 / 5000 = 6.00 × 10⁻³ A. With τ = RC = 0.600 s, I(t) = I₀ e^(−t/τ) = 1.81 × 10⁻³ A.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses (V₀/R)(1 − e^(−t/RC)), mistakenly thinking RC current grows toward V₀/R instead of decaying exponentially from V₀/R.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Stops at the initial peak current I₀ = V₀/R without applying exponential decay e^(−t/RC).

items.workedSolution: V_s = 800 V; P_out = V_s² / R_L = 5.33 × 10⁴ W. Input power P_in = P_out / η = 5.93 × 10⁴ W, so power loss P_loss = P_in − P_out = 5.93 × 10³ W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates P_in = P_out/η and P_loss = P_in − P_out = 5.93 × 10³ W (B).

items.stem: Ions of two carbon isotopes carrying charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C (m₁ = 1.99 × 10⁻²⁶ kg, m₂ = 2.32 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) emerge from the E = 4.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹, B₁ = 0.35 T selector of a environmental tracer Bainbridge instrument into a perpendicular B₂ = 0.7 T deflection chamber (out of the page). What is the straight-line separation ΔD between the two isotope strike marks on the detector wall?
items.workedSolution: Selected speed v = E / B₁ = 1.14 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. Semicircular strike separation ΔD = 2(r₂ − r₁) = 2(m₂ − m₁)E / (q B₁ B₂) = 6.73 × 10⁻³ m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses B₁² in the denominator instead of the product B₁B₂ of selector and chamber fields.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the difference in orbital radii |r₂ − r₁| and forgets the factor of 2 for semicircular impact diameters ΔD = 2|r₂ − r₁|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Reports the semicircular strike distance 2r₁ of the lighter isotope rather than the separation between isotopes.

markScheme.criterion: Includes negative sign of reversed field in N(B₂ − B₁)A.

items.stem: In the emergency-lighting fade circuit shown, a capacitor of capacitance C = 350 μF is first fully charged to V₀ = 12.0 V by closing Switch A while Switches B and C remain open. Switch A is then opened and Switch B is closed so the capacitor discharges through R₁ = 40 kΩ for 9.00 s. At t = 9.00 s, while Switch B stays closed, Switch C is closed to connect R₂ = 40 kΩ in parallel with R₁ for a further 6.00 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) One farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates. (b)(i) τ₁ = R₁C = 14.00 s, so V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁) = 6.309 V ≈ 6.31 V (confirming 6.3 V). (b)(ii) R_eq = R₁R₂/(R₁+R₂) = 20.0 kΩ, giving τ₂ = R_eq C = 7.000 s ≈ 7.00 s. (b)(iii) V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂) = 2.678 V ≈ 2.68 V. (b)(iv) smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.

markScheme.criterion: Mentions charge stored per unit potential difference (coulombs per volt).
Complete SI unit definition: capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
Evaluates stage-1 time constant τ₁ = R₁C = 14.0 s.
Correctly substitutes V₀, t₁, and τ₁ into V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁).
Shows V₁ = 6.309 V (≥3 s.f.: 6.31 V), clearly matching 6.3 V.
Combines R₁ || R₂ = 20.0 kΩ and calculates τ₂ = R_eq C = 7.00 s.
Substitutes V₁ (accepting rounded prompt value on ECF), t₂, and τ₂ into V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂).
Correct final potential difference V₂ = 2.68 V.
States correctly that V₂ would be smaller (smaller/larger matching direction).
Explains via time constants in both stages: smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.

parts.prompt: Define the farad.
parts.expectedAnswer: The farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
workingSteps: Recall the unit definition linking electric charge in coulombs and potential difference in volts.

parts.prompt: Show clearly that after discharging through R₁ alone for 9.00 s, the potential difference across the capacitor is approximately 6.3 V.
parts.expectedAnswer: 6.309 V (which rounds to 6.31 V and 6.3 V)
workingSteps: Stage 1 time constant τ₁ = R₁ C = (40 × 10³ Ω) × (350 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 14.00 s.
Substitute into V₁ = V₀ exp(−t₁ / τ₁) = 12.00 V × exp(−9 / 14.00 s).
Evaluate to 4 s.f.: V₁ = 6.309 V ≈ 6.31 V (confirming approximately 6.3 V).

parts.prompt: At the instant Switch C closes, calculate the new time constant τ₂ of the discharge circuit.
workingSteps: Combined parallel resistance R_eq = (R₁ R₂)/(R₁ + R₂) = (40 × 40) / (40 + 40) = 20.0 kΩ.
New time constant τ₂ = R_eq C = (20 × 10³ Ω) × (350 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 7.000 s ≈ 7.00 s.

parts.prompt: Calculate the potential difference V₂ across the capacitor after a further 6.00 s with both Switch B and Switch C closed.
workingSteps: Start Stage 2 decay from V₁ = 6.309 V with time constant τ₂ = 7.000 s.

parts.prompt: Without calculation, state and explain how the final potential difference V₂ would change if resistor R₁ were replaced by a smaller resistor throughout the entire experiment.
parts.expectedAnswer: Replacing the first resistor with a smaller resistor gives a smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.
workingSteps: A smaller resistance changes both the initial discharge time constant and the combined parallel resistance in the same direction.
Link the altered time constants in both stages to the rate of exponential decay and the remaining potential difference.

items.stem: Capacitor C₁ (18 μF) carries an initial potential difference V₁ = 53 V inside a capacitive voltage-divider test fixture. Switch S is closed to link C₁ directly across capacitor C₂ (42 μF), which is initially uncharged.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Q_net = C₁V₁ + C₂V₂ before switch closure.
Divides conserved charge from (a) by C₁ + C₂.
Subtracts final stored energy ½(C₁ + C₂)V_f² from initial stored energy.

items.stem: In a laboratory dielectric-constant cell, a regulated DC supply applies 150 V across two flat parallel electrodes of effective area 1.5 m² spaced 4.00 × 10⁻⁴ m apart. The space between the electrodes is filled uniformly by nylon spacer of relative permittivity 7.5 (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). What magnitude of charge is stored on each conducting plate?
items.workedSolution: Capacitance C = εᵣε₀A / d = 2.49 × 10⁻⁷ F. Plate charge Q = CV = 2.49 × 10⁻⁷ × 150 = 3.73 × 10⁻⁵ C.

markScheme.criterion: Combines C = εᵣε₀A/d with Q = CV to obtain 3.73 × 10⁻⁵ C (D).

items.stem: Within a secondary-ion mass analyser magnet, an electron carrying charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg gains kinetic energy across an accelerating voltage of 1200 V from rest and then curves in a uniform 5.00 × 10⁻³ T magnetic field (into the page). What is the radius of the resulting circular path inside the magnetic field?
items.workedSolution: From ½mv² = |q|V_acc, speed v = √(2|q|V_acc / m) = 2.05 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. Orbit radius r = mv / (|q|B) = (1/B)√(2mV_acc / |q|) = 0.0234 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 inside v = √(2|q|V_acc/m) from forgetting ½ in ½mv² = |q|V_acc.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Confuses orbital radius r with semicircular diameter 2r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates r² = 2mV_acc/(|q|B²) without taking the square root.

items.stem: During calibration of a capacitive MEMS accelerometer (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹), a 220 V supply charges parallel electrodes of area 0.45 m² spaced 2.40 × 10⁻⁴ m apart with relative permittivity 5.5. The electrodes are disconnected from the DC source so the plates remain electrically isolated, and the plate separation is then adjusted to 1.20 × 10⁻⁴ m at unchanged relative permittivity 5.5. What is the signed change in stored electrostatic energy ΔU = U_final − U_initial?
items.workedSolution: Initial C = 9.13 × 10⁻⁸ F and U_i = ½CV² = 2.21 × 10⁻³ J. Modified C′ = 1.83 × 10⁻⁷ F gives U_f = 1.10 × 10⁻³ J, so ΔU = U_f − U_i = −1.10 × 10⁻³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Determines U_i and U_f under the isolated-charge constraint to obtain ΔU = −1.10 × 10⁻³ J (A).

items.stem: Magnetic flux of density 4.80 × 10⁻³ T (directed into the page) pervades the vacuum region of a proton-therapy gantry bending magnet where an electron of mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg and charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C circulates at constant speed 2.10 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹ normal to the field lines. What is the radius of curvature r of the circular path?
items.workedSolution: Equating magnetic and centripetal forces |q|vB = mv²/r gives r = mv / (|q|B) = (9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg × 2.10 × 10⁷) / (0 × 4.80 × 10⁻³) = 0.0249 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Confuses orbital radius r = mv/(|q|B) with semicircular orbit diameter D = 2r.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the cyclotron radius formula and evaluates |q|B / (mv) instead of mv / (|q|B).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses mv²/(|q|B) by forgetting to cancel one power of speed v when equating mv²/r = |q|vB.

items.stem: An atomic-physics crossed-E/B beam gate combines parallel electrodes 0.04 m apart at 240 V (upper plate negative) with a crossed 0.32 T magnetic field (out of the page) for protons (q = +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) injected horizontally to the right at 1.13 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. At what speed would a proton instead have to enter this same selector to pass straight through undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Electric field E = V / d = 240 / 0.04 = 6.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹. Undeflected transmission requires qvB = qE, giving v_sel = E / B = 1.88 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.
