items.stem: In the flash-unit energy bank shown between terminals A and B, capacitor C₁ = 120 μF is connected in series with the parallel pair C₂ = 25 μF and C₃ = 35 μF. Every capacitor has a maximum safe working voltage of 40 V. What is the maximum safe potential difference that can be applied across terminals A and B without exceeding the rating of any capacitor?
items.workedSolution: Parallel pair C_p = C₂ + C₃ = 60 μF. Because C₁ (120 μF) and C_p (60 μF) carry equal series charge Q, the smaller capacitance (parallel pair of capacitors) reaches 40 V first. Thus V_AB,max = 40 × (1 + 60 / 120) = 60.00 V ≈ 60.0 V.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies that the parallel pair of capacitors limits the voltage and calculates V_AB,max = 60.0 V.

items.stem: An uncharged 50 μF capacitor in a camera shutter delay module is connected at switch closure in series with a 15 kΩ resistor across an ideal 9 V DC source and observed after 1.13 s.

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies resistance in Ω by capacitance in F (τ = RC).
Uses U = ½CV_C² with the voltage found in (b).

parts.prompt: Calculate the RC time constant τ of the circuit.
Determine the potential difference across the capacitor at t = 1.13 s.
Calculate the electrostatic energy stored in the capacitor at t = 1.13 s.

items.stem: In a tidal-stream rotor testbed, a rectangular coil of 200 turns and cross-sectional area 0.01 m² rotates steadily at 50 Hz inside a uniform 0.14 T magnetic field, passing through maximum flux linkage at t = 0 and sampled at t = 0.00167 s. What is the peak emf ε₀ generated by the rotating coil?
items.workedSolution: Angular speed ω = 2πf = 2π(50) = 314 rad s⁻¹. Peak emf ε₀ = NBAω = 200 × 0.14 × 0.01 × 314 = 88.0 V.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes single-turn peak emf BAω and omits multiplying by N turns.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes rotational frequency f directly into NBAω instead of angular speed ω = 2πf, omitting the 2π factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the amplitude and reports peak-to-peak emf 2ε₀ instead of peak emf ε₀.

items.stem: Parallel plates of length 0.06 m and gap 0.06 m in a time-of-flight ion-beam steerer are held at 1170 V. An electron of charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg enters midway between the plates parallel to their surfaces at 1.60 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. What is the resultant speed of the particle as it emerges from the plates?
items.workedSolution: Exit transverse speed |v_y| = (|q|VL)/(md v₀) = 1.28 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. Resultant speed v_exit = √(v₀² + v_y²) = 2.05 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates |v_y| and combines orthogonally v_exit = √(v₀² + v_y²) = 2.05 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: In an aircraft auxiliary AC bus resistive test rig, a winding of 220 turns and cross-sectional area 0.012 m² revolves at 50 Hz within a 0.16 T field and supplies sinusoidal AC directly to a 80 Ω resistive load. What root-mean-square (rms) current flows through the load resistor?
items.workedSolution: ε₀ = 2πfNBA = 133 V, so V_rms = ε₀ / √2 = 93.8 V. Load rms current I_rms = V_rms / R = 93.8 / 80 = 1.17 A.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 2π factor when converting frequency f into angular speed ω = 2πf.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates peak current I₀ = ε₀/R and omits dividing by √2 for rms current.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides peak current I₀ by 2 instead of √2.

items.stem: A high-resolution velocity-selected mass spectrograph filters magnesium ions (charge +3.20 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, masses m₁ = 3.98 × 10⁻²⁶ kg and m₂ = 4.32 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) using crossed fields E = 4.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ and B₁ = 0.35 T, then bends them through semicircular arcs onto a detector plate in a chamber field B₂ = 0.7 T (out of the page).

markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = m₁v / (qB₂) with chamber field B₂.
Doubles the radius difference ΔD = 2(r₂ − r₁).

parts.prompt: Calculate the common speed of the ions emerging from the velocity selector.
Determine the orbital radius r₁ of the lighter isotope in the deflection chamber.
Calculate the separation ΔD between the two isotope strike points on the detector wall.

items.stem: An accelerator quadrupole flux-integrator coil of 350 turns, area 0.004 m², and total circuit resistance 5 Ω sits perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field that reverses from B₁ = +0.35 T to B₂ = −0.210 T in 0.04 s. What is the magnitude of the average emf induced in the coil during the reversal?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates |ΔB| across sign reversal to obtain |ε| = 19.6 V (A).

items.stem: During a steady-state run on a drop-tower eddy-braking crossbar, a conducting rod of resistance 0.6 Ω glides right at 8 m s⁻¹ across rails 0.5 m apart bridged by 4.2 Ω in a 0.35 T magnetic field (directed out of the page). What induced current circulates around the closed loop?
items.workedSolution: Motional emf ε = BLv = 0.35 × 0.5 × 8 = 1.40 V. Loop current I = ε / (R + r) = 1.40 / 4.8 = 0.292 A.

items.stem: In the laboratory timer discharge board shown, a capacitor of capacitance C = 400 μF is first fully charged to V₀ = 12.0 V by closing Switch A while Switches B and C remain open. Switch A is then opened and Switch B is closed so the capacitor discharges through R₁ = 30 kΩ for 8.00 s. At t = 8.00 s, while Switch B stays closed, Switch C is closed to connect R₂ = 15 kΩ in parallel with R₁ for a further 4.00 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) One farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates. (b)(i) τ₁ = R₁C = 12.00 s, so V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁) = 6.161 V ≈ 6.16 V (confirming 6.2 V). (b)(ii) R_eq = R₁R₂/(R₁+R₂) = 10.0 kΩ, giving τ₂ = R_eq C = 4.000 s ≈ 4.00 s. (b)(iii) V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂) = 2.267 V ≈ 2.27 V. (b)(iv) smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.

markScheme.criterion: Mentions charge stored per unit potential difference (coulombs per volt).
Complete SI unit definition: capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
Evaluates stage-1 time constant τ₁ = R₁C = 12.0 s.
Correctly substitutes V₀, t₁, and τ₁ into V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁).
Shows V₁ = 6.161 V (≥3 s.f.: 6.16 V), clearly matching 6.2 V.
Combines R₁ || R₂ = 10.0 kΩ and calculates τ₂ = R_eq C = 4.00 s.
Substitutes V₁ (accepting rounded prompt value on ECF), t₂, and τ₂ into V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂).
Correct final potential difference V₂ = 2.27 V.
States correctly that V₂ would be smaller (smaller/larger matching direction).
Explains via time constants in both stages: smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.

parts.prompt: Define the farad.
parts.expectedAnswer: The farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
workingSteps: Recall the unit definition linking electric charge in coulombs and potential difference in volts.

parts.prompt: Show clearly that after discharging through R₁ alone for 8.00 s, the potential difference across the capacitor is approximately 6.2 V.
parts.expectedAnswer: 6.161 V (which rounds to 6.16 V and 6.2 V)
workingSteps: Stage 1 time constant τ₁ = R₁ C = (30 × 10³ Ω) × (400 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 12.00 s.
Substitute into V₁ = V₀ exp(−t₁ / τ₁) = 12.00 V × exp(−8 / 12.00 s).
Evaluate to 4 s.f.: V₁ = 6.161 V ≈ 6.16 V (confirming approximately 6.2 V).

parts.prompt: At the instant Switch C closes, calculate the new time constant τ₂ of the discharge circuit.
workingSteps: Combined parallel resistance R_eq = (R₁ R₂)/(R₁ + R₂) = (30 × 15) / (30 + 15) = 10.0 kΩ.
New time constant τ₂ = R_eq C = (10 × 10³ Ω) × (400 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 4.000 s ≈ 4.00 s.

parts.prompt: Calculate the potential difference V₂ across the capacitor after a further 4.00 s with both Switch B and Switch C closed.
workingSteps: Start Stage 2 decay from V₁ = 6.161 V with time constant τ₂ = 4.000 s.

parts.prompt: Without calculation, state and explain how the final potential difference V₂ would change if resistor R₁ were replaced by a smaller resistor throughout the entire experiment.
parts.expectedAnswer: Replacing the first resistor with a smaller resistor gives a smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.
workingSteps: A smaller resistance changes both the initial discharge time constant and the combined parallel resistance in the same direction.
Link the altered time constants in both stages to the rate of exponential decay and the remaining potential difference.

items.stem: In a capacitive voltage-divider test fixture, capacitor C₁ = 30 μF is charged to V₁ = 53 V, isolated from its supply, and then connected via switch S in parallel with capacitor C₂ = 50 μF (initially uncharged). What final common potential difference is established across both capacitors?
items.workedSolution: Total conserved charge Q_net = C₁V₁ + C₂V₂ = 1.59 × 10⁻³ C. Final parallel capacitance C_eq = 80 μF, so V_f = Q_net / (C₁ + C₂) = 19.9 V.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves net charge Q_net and divides by C₁ + C₂ to obtain 19.9 V (C).

items.stem: In a geophysical induction loop magnetometer, a flat winding of 80 turns, area 0.032 m², and circuit resistance 16 Ω sits in a magnetic field inclined at an angle of 55° with the normal to the coil. The magnetic flux density ramps uniformly from 0.22 T to 0.55 T over 0.025 s. What is the initial magnetic flux linkage NΦ₁ of the coil?
items.workedSolution: Angle to coil normal θ_n = 55°. Initial flux linkage NΦ₁ = NBA cos θ_n = 80 × 0.22 × 0.032 × cos 55° = 0.323 Wb.

markScheme.criterion: Uses θ_normal = 55° in NΦ₁ = NBA cos θ_normal to obtain 0.323 Wb (B).

items.stem: Starting at negligible speed in a sputter-source magnetic momentum filter, an electron (charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) traverses a 1200 V accelerating gap and enters a perpendicular 2.50 × 10⁻³ T magnetic field (out of the page).

markScheme.criterion: Uses ½mv² = |q|V_acc to solve for v.
Applies r = mv / (|q|B) using v from (a).
Multiplies orbital radius from (b) by two.

items.stem: During calibration of a high-voltage plate-separation apparatus (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹), a 100 V supply charges parallel electrodes of area 0.25 m² spaced 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ m apart with relative permittivity 3.5. The electrodes are disconnected from the DC source so the plates remain electrically isolated, and the plate separation is then adjusted to 0.001 m at unchanged relative permittivity 3.5.

markScheme.criterion: Finds initial C = εᵣε₀A/d and applies U_i = ½CV².
Evaluates C′ = εᵣε₀A / d′ at the new separation.
Uses constant charge U_f = Q²/(2C′) and subtracts U_i.

items.stem: A 31 V DC power supply energises a series combination of capacitor C₁ = 30 μF and capacitor C₂ = 90 μF inside a solar inverter buffer stage. What is the total equivalent capacitance of the series pair?
items.workedSolution: For series capacitors, 1/C_eq = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂, giving C_eq = (30 × 90)/(30 + 90) μF = 2.25 × 10⁻⁵ F.

options.distractorRationale: Treats series capacitors like series resistors by adding C₁ + C₂ directly instead of adding reciprocals.

options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the two capacitances |C₂ − C₁| instead of using (1/C₁ + 1/C₂)⁻¹.

items.stem: The defibrillator training board shown between terminals A and B combines C₁ = 240 μF in series with the parallel pair C₂ = 50 μF and C₃ = 30 μF. Each individual capacitor is rated to a maximum safe working potential difference of 40 V.
items.workedSolution: (a) C_p = 80 μF, C_eq = 60.00 μF ≈ 60.0 μF. (b) The parallel pair of capacitors hits 40 V first, giving V_AB,max = 53.33 V ≈ 53.3 V. (c) E_max = ½ C_eq V_AB,max² = 0.08533 J ≈ 0.0853 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies equal series charge Q and that the parallel pair of capacitors reaches 40 V first.

parts.prompt: Calculate the combined capacitance of the network between A and B in μF.
workingSteps: Parallel branch: C_p = C₂ + C₃ = 50 + 30 = 80 μF.
Series combination: C_eq = (C₁ C_p) / (C₁ + C_p) = (240 × 80) / (240 + 80) = 60.00 μF ≈ 60.0 μF.

parts.prompt: Determine the maximum safe potential difference that can be applied across A and B, stating which section reaches its voltage rating first.
parts.expectedAnswer: 53.3 V (limited by the parallel pair of capacitors)
workingSteps: In series both sections hold equal charge Q, so V ∝ 1/C; the smaller capacitance (parallel pair of capacitors) reaches 40 V first.
Maximum safe total pd V_AB,max = 40 × (1 + 80 / 240) = 53.33 V ≈ 53.3 V.

parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum electrical energy safely stored in the complete network.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Reports the RC time constant τ = RC (36.8% decay time) instead of multiplying by ln 2 for 50% decay.

markScheme.criterion: Uses E = V/d and a = |q|E / m.
Finds transit time t = L/v₀ and applies |Δy| = ½ a t².
Evaluates |v_y| = a t and θ = arctan(|v_y| / v₀).

items.stem: In a marine diesel-electric AC load-testing unit, a winding of 140 turns and cross-sectional area 0.012 m² revolves at 50 Hz within a 0.16 T field and supplies sinusoidal AC directly to a 25 Ω resistive load.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P_mean = I_rms² R (= ½ ε₀ I₀).

Determine the rms current in the resistive load.
Calculate the mean electrical power dissipated in the load.

items.stem: In a nuclear-forensics Bainbridge analyser, two chlorine isotopes of equal charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and masses m₁ = 5.81 × 10⁻²⁶ kg and m₂ = 6.14 × 10⁻²⁶ kg pass undeflected through a velocity selector (E = 6.80 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹, B₁ = 0.35 T) before entering a semicircular analyser chamber with uniform field B₂ = 0.7 T (out of the page). What is the orbital radius r₁ of the lighter isotope inside the deflection chamber?
items.workedSolution: Selector speed v = E / B₁ = 1.94 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. In chamber field B₂, r₁ = m₁v / (qB₂) = m₁E / (qB₁B₂) = 0.101 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by √2 through an inverted root-mean-square or kinetic-energy scaling.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Confuses orbital radius r₁ with semicircular impact diameter D₁ = 2r₁.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides E by B₂ instead of B₁ in the velocity selector, evaluating m₁E/(qB₂²).

items.stem: In the reservoir safety discharge rig shown, a capacitor of capacitance C = 680 μF is first fully charged to V₀ = 9.60 V by closing Switch A while Switches B and C remain open. Switch A is then opened and Switch B is closed so the capacitor discharges through R₁ = 30 kΩ for 15.0 s. At t = 15.0 s, while Switch B stays closed, Switch C is closed to connect R₂ = 15 kΩ in parallel with R₁ for a further 6.00 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) One farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates. (b)(i) τ₁ = R₁C = 20.40 s, so V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁) = 4.602 V ≈ 4.60 V (confirming 4.6 V). (b)(ii) R_eq = R₁R₂/(R₁+R₂) = 10.0 kΩ, giving τ₂ = R_eq C = 6.800 s ≈ 6.80 s. (b)(iii) V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂) = 1.904 V ≈ 1.90 V. (b)(iv) smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.

markScheme.criterion: Mentions charge stored per unit potential difference (coulombs per volt).
Complete SI unit definition: capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
Evaluates stage-1 time constant τ₁ = R₁C = 20.4 s.
Correctly substitutes V₀, t₁, and τ₁ into V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁).
Shows V₁ = 4.602 V (≥3 s.f.: 4.60 V), clearly matching 4.6 V.
Combines R₁ || R₂ = 10.0 kΩ and calculates τ₂ = R_eq C = 6.80 s.
Substitutes V₁ (accepting rounded prompt value on ECF), t₂, and τ₂ into V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂).
Correct final potential difference V₂ = 1.90 V.
States correctly that V₂ would be smaller (smaller/larger matching direction).
Explains via time constants in both stages: smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.

parts.prompt: Define the farad.
parts.expectedAnswer: The farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
workingSteps: Recall the unit definition linking electric charge in coulombs and potential difference in volts.

parts.prompt: Show clearly that after discharging through R₁ alone for 15.0 s, the potential difference across the capacitor is approximately 4.6 V.
parts.expectedAnswer: 4.602 V (which rounds to 4.60 V and 4.6 V)
workingSteps: Stage 1 time constant τ₁ = R₁ C = (30 × 10³ Ω) × (680 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 20.40 s.
Substitute into V₁ = V₀ exp(−t₁ / τ₁) = 9.600 V × exp(−15 / 20.40 s).
Evaluate to 4 s.f.: V₁ = 4.602 V ≈ 4.60 V (confirming approximately 4.6 V).

parts.prompt: At the instant Switch C closes, calculate the new time constant τ₂ of the discharge circuit.
workingSteps: Combined parallel resistance R_eq = (R₁ R₂)/(R₁ + R₂) = (30 × 15) / (30 + 15) = 10.0 kΩ.
New time constant τ₂ = R_eq C = (10 × 10³ Ω) × (680 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 6.800 s ≈ 6.80 s.

parts.prompt: Calculate the potential difference V₂ across the capacitor after a further 6.00 s with both Switch B and Switch C closed.
workingSteps: Start Stage 2 decay from V₁ = 4.602 V with time constant τ₂ = 6.800 s.

parts.prompt: Without calculation, state and explain how the final potential difference V₂ would change if resistor R₁ were replaced by a smaller resistor throughout the entire experiment.
parts.expectedAnswer: Replacing the first resistor with a smaller resistor gives a smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.
workingSteps: A smaller resistance changes both the initial discharge time constant and the combined parallel resistance in the same direction.
Link the altered time constants in both stages to the rate of exponential decay and the remaining potential difference.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Q_net = C₁V₁ + C₂V₂ before switch closure.
Divides conserved charge from (a) by C₁ + C₂.
Subtracts final stored energy ½(C₁ + C₂)V_f² from initial stored energy.

items.stem: Accelerated from rest through 2400 V in a Thomson e/m specific-charge apparatus, a singly ionised lithium ion of charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 1.16 × 10⁻²⁶ kg passes into a uniform 0.450 T magnetic field directed into the page at right angles to its velocity. What speed does the particle reach upon entering the magnetic field?
items.workedSolution: Equating ½mv² = |q|V_acc gives v = √(2|q|V_acc / m) = √(2 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ × 2400 / 1.16 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) = 2.57 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Forgets the ½ in ½mv² = |q|V_acc and computes √(|q|V_acc / m).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by 4 instead of 2 inside the square root.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes v² = 2|q|V_acc / m without taking the square root.

items.stem: An experimental dielectric displacement gauge features plates of area 1 m² at initial spacing 3.00 × 10⁻⁴ m filled with a medium of relative permittivity 4.8 and charged to 180 V (take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). The plates are disconnected from the DC source so the plates remain electrically isolated, and the plate separation is then adjusted to 6.00 × 10⁻⁴ m while εᵣ stays at 4.8. What is the new potential difference across the isolated plates?
items.workedSolution: For isolated plates, charge Q is conserved while C′ = C₀(d/d′). Therefore V′ = Q / C′ = V₀(d′/d) = 180 × (0.0006 / 0.0003) = 360 V.

markScheme.criterion: Uses charge conservation V′ = V₀(d′/d) to obtain 360 V (B).

items.stem: Within a vacuum Wien crossed-field velocity filter, a proton (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally along the central axis between plates 0.015 m apart at p.d. 240 V (upper plate positive) inside a perpendicular 0.12 T field (into the page). At what speed must the proton travel to pass straight through the exit slit undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Uniform electric field E = V / d = 240 / 0.015 = 1.60 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. Zero net deflection requires qE = qvB, so v_sel = E / B = V / (Bd) = 1.33 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_sel = V / (Bd) to obtain 1.33 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: In the pulse-forming network shown between terminals A and B, capacitor C₁ = 180 μF is connected in series with the parallel pair C₂ = 20 μF and C₃ = 40 μF. Every capacitor has a maximum safe working voltage of 25 V. What is the maximum safe potential difference that can be applied across terminals A and B without exceeding the rating of any capacitor?
items.workedSolution: Parallel pair C_p = C₂ + C₃ = 60 μF. Because C₁ (180 μF) and C_p (60 μF) carry equal series charge Q, the smaller capacitance (parallel pair of capacitors) reaches 25 V first. Thus V_AB,max = 25 × (1 + 60 / 180) = 33.33 V ≈ 33.3 V.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies that the parallel pair of capacitors limits the voltage and calculates V_AB,max = 33.3 V.

items.stem: Rotating uniformly at 25 Hz in a 0.35 T magnetic field, the coil (150 turns, area 0.03 m²) of a laboratory hand-cranked slip-ring coil starts at peak flux linkage at t = 0 and reaches t = 0.00667 s. What is the peak-to-peak emf displayed on an oscilloscope across one full cycle?
items.workedSolution: Peak emf ε₀ = 2πfNBA = 247 V. Peak-to-peak emf V_pp = 2ε₀ = 495 V.

items.stem: During calibration of an electron-beam lithography electrostatic deflector, a collimated proton beam (charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) enters at 5.80 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ along the central axis of 0.075 m long parallel electrodes separated by 0.05 m at p.d. 968 V. What is the magnitude of the transverse deflection as the particle exits the plates?
items.workedSolution: Transit time t = L / v₀ = 0.075 / 5.80 × 10⁵ = 1.29 × 10⁻⁷ s. Transverse acceleration a_y = |q|V / (md) = 1.85 × 10¹² m s⁻². Deflection |Δy| = ½ a_y t² = 0.0155 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t = L/v₀, a_y = |q|V/(md), and |Δy| = ½a_y t² = 0.0155 m (C).

items.stem: A laboratory bench variac step-down core with 1600 primary turns and 80 secondary turns operates at an efficiency of 0.95 (95%) from a 500 V rms AC supply while driving a 32 Ω resistive secondary load. What rms current is drawn from the primary AC supply?
items.workedSolution: Secondary rms voltage V_s = V_p(N_s/N_p) = 500(80/1600) = 25.0 V. Output power P_out = V_s² / R_L = 19.5 W. Input power P_in = P_out / η = 20.6 W, so I_p = P_in / V_p = 0.0411 A.

markScheme.criterion: Computes V_s, P_out, and I_p = P_out / (η V_p) = 0.0411 A (C).

items.stem: In a laboratory slip-ring alternator with ohmic load, a winding of 280 turns and cross-sectional area 0.025 m² revolves at 50 Hz within a 0.16 T field and supplies sinusoidal AC directly to a 40 Ω resistive load. What mean electrical power is dissipated in the resistive load over a complete cycle?
items.workedSolution: Peak emf ε₀ = 2πfNBA = 352 V; V_rms = ε₀ / √2 = 249 V. Mean resistive power P_mean = V_rms² / R = ½ ε₀² / R = 1.55 × 10³ W.

markScheme.criterion: Computes ε₀ = 2πfNBA and mean power P_mean = ½ε₀²/R = 1.55 × 10³ W (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides peak power V₀I₀ by √2 instead of 2, forgetting that both V_rms = V₀/√2 and I_rms = I₀/√2 contribute a 1/√2 factor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates peak instantaneous power V₀²/R without applying the ½ sinusoidal average factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides V₀ by 2 instead of √2 before squaring in V_rms²/R, introducing a ¼ factor.

items.stem: Entering through collimator slit S after undeflected passage across E = 4.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ and B₁ = 0.35 T in a medical stable-isotope Bainbridge sector, potassium ions (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C; masses 6.47 × 10⁻²⁶ kg and 6.81 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) describe semicircular trajectories in a 0.7 T field (out of the page). What is the straight-line separation ΔD between the two isotope strike marks on the detector wall?
items.workedSolution: Selected speed v = E / B₁ = 1.14 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. Semicircular strike separation ΔD = 2(r₂ − r₁) = 2(m₂ − m₁)E / (q B₁ B₂) = 6.94 × 10⁻³ m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses B₁² in the denominator instead of the product B₁B₂ of selector and chamber fields.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Reports the semicircular strike distance 2r₁ of the lighter isotope rather than the separation between isotopes.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the difference in orbital radii |r₂ − r₁| and forgets the factor of 2 for semicircular impact diameters ΔD = 2|r₂ − r₁|.

items.stem: Aligned normal to the axis of an electromagnet, a palaeomagnetic core-sample pickup loop (75 turns, area 0.01 m², loop resistance 12 Ω) experiences a polarity reversal from +0.8 T to −0.800 T over 0.08 s. What total magnitude of electric charge ΔQ flows around the circuit during this reversal?
items.workedSolution: Signed field change |ΔB| = |-0.8 − 0.8| = 1.6 T, so |Δ(NΦ)| = 75 × 1.6 × 0.01 = 1.20 Wb. Induced charge ΔQ = |Δ(NΦ)| / R = 0.100 C.

markScheme.criterion: Accounts for field sign reversal in |Δ(NΦ)| and evaluates ΔQ = |Δ(NΦ)|/R = 0.100 C (D).

items.stem: On a space-tether electrodynamic rail rig, a conducting bar of internal resistance 0.8 Ω slides to the left at a steady speed of 4 m s⁻¹ along parallel horizontal rails of negligible resistance spaced 0.2 m apart. A uniform 0.75 T magnetic field (directed into the page) threads the rails, which are bridged by a 1.4 Ω load resistor. What external pulling force magnitude is needed to maintain this constant speed?
items.workedSolution: Motional emf ε = BLv = 0.600 V. Total loop resistance R_tot = 1.4 + 0.8 = 2.2 Ω, giving I = ε / R_tot = 0.273 A. Pulling force F = BIL = 0.0409 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ε = BLv, I = ε/(R + r), and F = BIL = 0.0409 N (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes mechanical input power P = Fv instead of the applied pulling force F.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Stops after evaluating the induced loop current I = BLv/(R + r) without multiplying by B L.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Neglects the internal resistance of the moving rod and divides by the external load resistance R alone.

items.stem: In the two-branch RC discharge network shown, a capacitor of capacitance C = 450 μF is first fully charged to V₀ = 13.5 V by closing Switch A while Switches B and C remain open. Switch A is then opened and Switch B is closed so the capacitor discharges through R₁ = 30 kΩ for 10.0 s. At t = 10.0 s, while Switch B stays closed, Switch C is closed to connect R₂ = 15 kΩ in parallel with R₁ for a further 4.50 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) One farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates. (b)(i) τ₁ = R₁C = 13.50 s, so V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁) = 6.436 V ≈ 6.44 V (confirming 6.4 V). (b)(ii) R_eq = R₁R₂/(R₁+R₂) = 10.0 kΩ, giving τ₂ = R_eq C = 4.500 s ≈ 4.50 s. (b)(iii) V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂) = 2.368 V ≈ 2.37 V. (b)(iv) larger final potential difference because the time constant increases and the capacitor discharges more slowly.

markScheme.criterion: Mentions charge stored per unit potential difference (coulombs per volt).
Complete SI unit definition: capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
Evaluates stage-1 time constant τ₁ = R₁C = 13.5 s.
Correctly substitutes V₀, t₁, and τ₁ into V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁).
Shows V₁ = 6.436 V (≥3 s.f.: 6.44 V), clearly matching 6.4 V.
Combines R₁ || R₂ = 10.0 kΩ and calculates τ₂ = R_eq C = 4.50 s.
Substitutes V₁ (accepting rounded prompt value on ECF), t₂, and τ₂ into V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂).
Correct final potential difference V₂ = 2.37 V.
States correctly that V₂ would be larger (smaller/larger matching direction).
Explains via time constants in both stages: larger final potential difference because the time constant increases and the capacitor discharges more slowly.

parts.prompt: Define the farad.
parts.expectedAnswer: The farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
workingSteps: Recall the unit definition linking electric charge in coulombs and potential difference in volts.

parts.prompt: Show clearly that after discharging through R₁ alone for 10.0 s, the potential difference across the capacitor is approximately 6.4 V.
parts.expectedAnswer: 6.436 V (which rounds to 6.44 V and 6.4 V)
workingSteps: Stage 1 time constant τ₁ = R₁ C = (30 × 10³ Ω) × (450 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 13.50 s.
Substitute into V₁ = V₀ exp(−t₁ / τ₁) = 13.50 V × exp(−10 / 13.50 s).
Evaluate to 4 s.f.: V₁ = 6.436 V ≈ 6.44 V (confirming approximately 6.4 V).

parts.prompt: At the instant Switch C closes, calculate the new time constant τ₂ of the discharge circuit.
workingSteps: Combined parallel resistance R_eq = (R₁ R₂)/(R₁ + R₂) = (30 × 15) / (30 + 15) = 10.0 kΩ.
New time constant τ₂ = R_eq C = (10 × 10³ Ω) × (450 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 4.500 s ≈ 4.50 s.

parts.prompt: Calculate the potential difference V₂ across the capacitor after a further 4.50 s with both Switch B and Switch C closed.
workingSteps: Start Stage 2 decay from V₁ = 6.436 V with time constant τ₂ = 4.500 s.

parts.prompt: Without calculation, state and explain how the final potential difference V₂ would change if resistor R₁ were replaced by a larger resistor throughout the entire experiment.
parts.expectedAnswer: Replacing the first resistor with a larger resistor gives a larger final potential difference because the time constant increases and the capacitor discharges more slowly.
workingSteps: A larger resistance changes both the initial discharge time constant and the combined parallel resistance in the same direction.
Link the altered time constants in both stages to the rate of exponential decay and the remaining potential difference.

items.stem: Capacitor C₁ (20 μF) carries an initial potential difference V₁ = 23 V inside a switched-capacitor sample-and-hold stage. Switch S is closed to link C₁ directly across capacitor C₂ (80 μF), which is initially uncharged. How much electrostatic energy is dissipated in the connecting leads as equilibrium is reached?
items.workedSolution: Initial energy U_i = 5.29 × 10⁻³ J. Final common voltage V_f = 4.60 V gives final energy U_f = ½(C₁ + C₂)V_f² = 1.06 × 10⁻³ J. Energy dissipated ΔU = U_i − U_f = 4.23 × 10⁻³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates U_i − U_f after conserving charge to obtain 4.23 × 10⁻³ J (B).

items.stem: During a dielectric bench test, a polyimide sheet sheet with relative permittivity 4.4 completely fills the 2.00 × 10⁻⁴ m gap between parallel metal plates of area 0.6 m² inside an aerospace humidity-compensated sensor. When the assembly is charged to 320 V (take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹), calculate the energy stored per unit volume inside the dielectric.
items.workedSolution: Uniform field E = V / d = 320 / 0.0002 = 1.60 × 10⁶ V m⁻¹. Energy density u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² = 0.5 × 4.4 × 8.85 × 10⁻¹² × (1.60 × 10⁶)² = 49.8 J m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = V/d and u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² to obtain 49.8 J m⁻³ (C).

items.stem: Maintaining an angle of 20° with the normal to the coil, the magnetic field threading a wireless inductive telemetry receiver coil with 240 turns and area 0.008 m² (total resistance 16 Ω) decays uniformly from 0.56 T to zero in 0.1 s. What average induced current circulates around the closed coil during the ramp?
items.workedSolution: With θ_normal = 20°, |ε| = N|ΔB|A cos 20° / Δt = 10.1 V. Average current I = |ε| / R = 10.1 / 16 = 0.631 A.

markScheme.criterion: Computes |ε| using θ_normal = 20° and I = |ε|/R = 0.631 A (C).

items.stem: Starting at negligible speed in a isotopic beam-separator bending magnet, a doubly ionised magnesium ion (charge +3.20 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 3.98 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) traverses a 1000 V accelerating gap and enters a perpendicular 0.550 T magnetic field (into the page). If the particle completes a semicircular turn onto an exit detector plate, what is the strike diameter D from the entry slit?
items.workedSolution: Speed v = √(2|q|V_acc / m) = 1.27 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹; radius r = mv / (|q|B) = 0.0287 m. Semicircular detector separation D = 2r = 0.0574 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in v = √(2|q|V_acc/m) when computing r before doubling.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes curved semicircular arc length πr rather than straight-line detector chord 2r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Reports the orbital radius r = (1/B)√(2mV_acc/|q|) instead of the semicircular chord diameter D = 2r.

items.stem: A variable-gap precision electrometer has plate area 0.45 m², initial separation 6.00 × 10⁻⁴ m, and relative permittivity 6.5, energised initially at 220 V (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). Next, the assembly is kept connected across the DC source at constant potential difference while the plate separation is adjusted to 9.00 × 10⁻⁴ m with εᵣ = 6.5 throughout. What is the final electrostatic energy stored in the modified state?
items.workedSolution: Initial capacitance C = 4.31 × 10⁻⁸ F, modified capacitance C′ = 2.88 × 10⁻⁸ F. Under constant-voltage, final stored energy U′ = 6.96 × 10⁻⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes modified capacitance C′ and evaluates final stored energy 6.96 × 10⁻⁴ J (C).

items.stem: Across a 7 V DC bus in an audio crossover filter module, capacitor C_s (40 μF) lies in series with the parallel combination of C_p1 (15 μF) and C_p2 (25 μF). What total electrostatic energy is stored in the complete network?
items.workedSolution: Parallel bank C_p = 40 μF; total C_eq = 2.00 × 10⁻⁵ F. Stored energy U = ½C_eq V₀² = 0.5 × 2.00 × 10⁻⁵ × (7)² = 4.90 × 10⁻⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates C_eq and computes U = ½C_eq V₀² = 4.90 × 10⁻⁴ J (A).

items.stem: During a beam run in a synchrotron dipole bending sector, an electron carrying charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg moves at 2.60 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹ normal to a 3.50 × 10⁻³ T field directed out of the page. What is the radius of curvature r of the circular path?
items.workedSolution: Equating magnetic and centripetal forces |q|vB = mv²/r gives r = mv / (|q|B) = (9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg × 2.60 × 10⁷) / (0 × 3.50 × 10⁻³) = 0.0423 m.

options.distractorRationale: Confuses orbital radius r = mv/(|q|B) with semicircular orbit diameter D = 2r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the cyclotron radius formula and evaluates |q|B / (mv) instead of mv / (|q|B).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses mv²/(|q|B) by forgetting to cancel one power of speed v when equating mv²/r = |q|vB.

items.stem: Crossed fields in an atomic-physics crossed-E/B beam gate are produced by 900 V across plates spaced 0.025 m apart (upper plate negative) and a 0.32 T field directed out of the page; a proton (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally to the right at 6.75 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. What is the initial upward transverse acceleration of the proton upon entering the crossed fields?
items.workedSolution: E = V/d = 3.60 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. Upward electric force F_E = qE = 5.76 × 10⁻¹⁵ N; downward magnetic force |F_B| = qvB = 3.46 × 10⁻¹⁵ N. Net upward acceleration a_y = (F_E − |F_B|) / m = 1.38 × 10¹² m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing qvB from qE and divides by m to obtain 1.38 × 10¹² m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: In the rectifier reservoir block shown between terminals A and B, capacitor C₁ = 150 μF is connected in series with the parallel pair C₂ = 45 μF and C₃ = 30 μF. Every capacitor has a maximum safe working voltage of 50 V. What is the maximum safe potential difference that can be applied across terminals A and B without exceeding the rating of any capacitor?
items.workedSolution: Parallel pair C_p = C₂ + C₃ = 75 μF. Because C₁ (150 μF) and C_p (75 μF) carry equal series charge Q, the smaller capacitance (parallel pair of capacitors) reaches 50 V first. Thus V_AB,max = 50 × (1 + 75 / 150) = 75.00 V ≈ 75.0 V.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies that the parallel pair of capacitors limits the voltage and calculates V_AB,max = 75.0 V.

items.stem: An uncharged 100 μF capacitor in a laboratory data-logger discharge rig is connected at switch closure in series with a 15 kΩ resistor across an ideal 6 V DC source and observed after 0.6 s. How much electrostatic energy is stored in the capacitor at t = 0.6 s?
items.workedSolution: τ = RC = 1.50 s, giving V_C(0.6 s) = 1.98 V. Stored energy U = ½CV_C² = 0.5 × 1.00 × 10⁻⁴ × (1.98)² = 1.96 × 10⁻⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V_C(t) and computes U(t) = ½CV_C(t)² = 1.96 × 10⁻⁴ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates maximum stored energy ½CV₀² rather than the instantaneous energy at the query time.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Forgets the factor of one-half in U(t) = ½CV_C(t)².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Scales stored energy linearly with V_C(t)/V₀ instead of quadratically with (V_C(t)/V₀)² in U = ½CV_C².

items.stem: During testing of a portable Diesel-coupled AC armature, a coil with 120 turns and area 0.018 m² revolves at 100 Hz in a 0.14 T field, starting perpendicular to the field lines at t = 0 and queried at t = 8.33 × 10⁻⁴ s. What instantaneous emf ε is induced at t = 8.33 × 10⁻⁴ s?
items.workedSolution: ω = 2π(100) = 628 rad s⁻¹, ε₀ = NBAω = 190 V. At t = 8.33 × 10⁻⁴ s, ε(t) = ε₀ sin(ωt) = 95.0 V.

markScheme.criterion: Computes ε₀ = 2πfNBA and evaluates ε₀ sin(ωt) = 95.0 V (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reports the maximum amplitude ε₀ rather than evaluating ε(t) = ε₀ sin(ωt) at the specified instant.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates ε₀ cos(ωt) instead of ε₀ sin(ωt), confusing the phase of induced emf with magnetic flux linkage.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits 2π when computing peak amplitude NBAω before multiplying by sin(ωt).

items.stem: Projected horizontally into an electrostatic cathode-ray oscilloscope tube at speed 5.00 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹, a proton (mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg, charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) experiences the uniform field between 0.09 m parallel plates spaced 0.06 m apart at 789 V. What is the resultant speed of the particle as it emerges from the plates?
items.workedSolution: Exit transverse speed |v_y| = (|q|VL)/(md v₀) = 2.27 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. Resultant speed v_exit = √(v₀² + v_y²) = 5.49 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates |v_y| and combines orthogonally v_exit = √(v₀² + v_y²) = 5.49 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Across a pure 25 Ω load in a wind-turbine test generator driving a load bank, a coil of 140 turns and area 0.025 m² (negligible coil resistance) rotates uniformly at 40 Hz inside a 0.38 T magnetic field. What is the root-mean-square (rms) potential difference across the load?
items.workedSolution: Peak emf ε₀ = 2πfNBA = 2π(40)(140)(0.38)(0.025) = 334 V. Therefore V_rms = ε₀ / √2 = 236 V.

markScheme.criterion: Finds ε₀ = 2πfNBA and divides by √2 to obtain 236 V (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies peak emf ε₀ by √2 instead of dividing by √2.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Stops at peak emf ε₀ = 2πfNBA without dividing by √2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides peak emf ε₀ by 2 (confusing the ½ power factor with the 1/√2 rms voltage factor).

items.stem: Within a high-resolution velocity-selected mass spectrograph, crossed selector fields E = 6.80 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ and B₁ = 0.25 T admit neon isotopes of charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and masses m₁ = 3.32 × 10⁻²⁶ kg and m₂ = 3.65 × 10⁻²⁶ kg through slit S into a uniform B₂ = 0.6 T magnetic sector (into the page). What is the orbital radius r₁ of the lighter isotope inside the deflection chamber?
items.workedSolution: Selector speed v = E / B₁ = 2.72 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. In chamber field B₂, r₁ = m₁v / (qB₂) = m₁E / (qB₁B₂) = 0.0941 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides E by B₂ instead of B₁ in the velocity selector, evaluating m₁E/(qB₂²).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses B₁ in the deflection chamber instead of B₂, evaluating m₁E/(qB₁²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Confuses orbital radius r₁ with semicircular impact diameter D₁ = 2r₁.

items.stem: In a magnetic calibration run, the axial flux density perpendicular to a cryogenic solenoid quench-sensing coil with 180 turns, cross-section 0.022 m², and resistance 2 Ω switches from +0.25 T to −0.150 T during an interval of 0.2 s. What is the magnitude of the average emf induced in the coil during the reversal?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates |ΔB| across sign reversal to obtain |ε| = 7.92 V (B).

items.stem: During a steady-state run on a space-tether electrodynamic rail rig, a conducting rod of resistance 0.4 Ω glides right at 8 m s⁻¹ across rails 0.5 m apart bridged by 4.2 Ω in a 1.25 T magnetic field (directed out of the page). What is the terminal potential difference across the external load resistor?
items.workedSolution: ε = BLv = 5.00 V; loop current I = ε / (R + r) = 1.09 A. Terminal p.d. across load V_term = I R = 1.09 × 4.2 = 4.57 V.

markScheme.criterion: Uses V_term = BLv × R/(R + r) to obtain 4.57 V (B).

items.stem: In the switched RC demonstration panel shown, a capacitor of capacitance C = 400 μF is first fully charged to V₀ = 7.50 V by closing Switch A while Switches B and C remain open. Switch A is then opened and Switch B is closed so the capacitor discharges through R₁ = 40 kΩ for 10.0 s. At t = 10.0 s, while Switch B stays closed, Switch C is closed to connect R₂ = 40 kΩ in parallel with R₁ for a further 7.00 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) One farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates. (b)(i) τ₁ = R₁C = 16.00 s, so V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁) = 4.014 V ≈ 4.01 V (confirming 4.0 V). (b)(ii) R_eq = R₁R₂/(R₁+R₂) = 20.0 kΩ, giving τ₂ = R_eq C = 8.000 s ≈ 8.00 s. (b)(iii) V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂) = 1.673 V ≈ 1.67 V. (b)(iv) smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.

markScheme.criterion: Mentions charge stored per unit potential difference (coulombs per volt).
Complete SI unit definition: capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
Evaluates stage-1 time constant τ₁ = R₁C = 16.0 s.
Correctly substitutes V₀, t₁, and τ₁ into V₁ = V₀ e^(−t₁/τ₁).
Shows V₁ = 4.014 V (≥3 s.f.: 4.01 V), clearly matching 4.0 V.
Combines R₁ || R₂ = 20.0 kΩ and calculates τ₂ = R_eq C = 8.00 s.
Substitutes V₁ (accepting rounded prompt value on ECF), t₂, and τ₂ into V₂ = V₁ e^(−t₂/τ₂).
Correct final potential difference V₂ = 1.67 V.
States correctly that V₂ would be smaller (smaller/larger matching direction).
Explains via time constants in both stages: smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.

parts.prompt: Define the farad.
parts.expectedAnswer: The farad is the capacitance that stores one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference across the plates.
workingSteps: Recall the unit definition linking electric charge in coulombs and potential difference in volts.

parts.prompt: Show clearly that after discharging through R₁ alone for 10.0 s, the potential difference across the capacitor is approximately 4.0 V.
parts.expectedAnswer: 4.014 V (which rounds to 4.01 V and 4.0 V)
workingSteps: Stage 1 time constant τ₁ = R₁ C = (40 × 10³ Ω) × (400 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 16.00 s.
Substitute into V₁ = V₀ exp(−t₁ / τ₁) = 7.500 V × exp(−10 / 16.00 s).
Evaluate to 4 s.f.: V₁ = 4.014 V ≈ 4.01 V (confirming approximately 4.0 V).

parts.prompt: At the instant Switch C closes, calculate the new time constant τ₂ of the discharge circuit.
workingSteps: Combined parallel resistance R_eq = (R₁ R₂)/(R₁ + R₂) = (40 × 40) / (40 + 40) = 20.0 kΩ.
New time constant τ₂ = R_eq C = (20 × 10³ Ω) × (400 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 8.000 s ≈ 8.00 s.

parts.prompt: Calculate the potential difference V₂ across the capacitor after a further 7.00 s with both Switch B and Switch C closed.
workingSteps: Start Stage 2 decay from V₁ = 4.014 V with time constant τ₂ = 8.000 s.

parts.prompt: Without calculation, state and explain how the final potential difference V₂ would change if resistor R₁ were replaced by a smaller resistor throughout the entire experiment.
parts.expectedAnswer: Replacing the first resistor with a smaller resistor gives a smaller final potential difference because the time constant decreases and the capacitor discharges more rapidly.
workingSteps: A smaller resistance changes both the initial discharge time constant and the combined parallel resistance in the same direction.
Link the altered time constants in both stages to the rate of exponential decay and the remaining potential difference.

items.stem: During a charge-conservation test on a pulsed laser pre-ioniser loop, C₁ = 12 μF at initial voltage V₁ = 17 V is connected by closing switch S across C₂ = 36 μF (initially uncharged). What final common potential difference is established across both capacitors?
items.workedSolution: Total conserved charge Q_net = C₁V₁ + C₂V₂ = 2.04 × 10⁻⁴ C. Final parallel capacitance C_eq = 48 μF, so V_f = Q_net / (C₁ + C₂) = 4.25 V.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves net charge Q_net and divides by C₁ + C₂ to obtain 4.25 V (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes all initial charge from C₁ transfers onto C₂ instead of splitting across C₁ + C₂.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Takes the unweighted average (V₁ + V₂)/2 without weighting by C₁ and C₂ via charge conservation.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides conserved net charge by series capacitance C₁C₂/(C₁ + C₂) instead of parallel C₁ + C₂.

items.stem: A ceramic capacitive pressure transducer consists of parallel conducting plates of overlapping area 0.24 m² separated by a uniform alumina ceramic layer of thickness 2.50 × 10⁻⁴ m and relative permittivity 3.8. A steady potential difference of 150 V is maintained across the plates (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). What electrostatic energy is stored in the capacitor?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates C = εᵣε₀A/d and U = ½CV² to obtain 3.63 × 10⁻⁴ J (D).

items.stem: An experimental synchrotron dipole field-monitoring coil comprises 120 closely wound turns of area 0.012 m² and resistance 5 Ω. Held at a fixed orientation where the field lines make an angle of 70° with the plane of the coil, the field ramps uniformly from 0.36 T to 1.08 T over 0.05 s. What is the magnitude of the average emf induced in the coil?

markScheme.criterion: Projects flux along coil normal (20°) and evaluates |ε| = N|ΔΦ|/Δt = 19.5 V (C).

items.stem: Before entering the uniform 0.250 T magnetic field (out of the page) of a nuclear astrophysics recoil separator at right angles, a singly ionised lithium ion (q = +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 1.16 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) is accelerated from rest through an electrode voltage of 800 V. What speed does the particle reach upon entering the magnetic field?
items.workedSolution: Equating ½mv² = |q|V_acc gives v = √(2|q|V_acc / m) = √(2 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ × 800 / 1.16 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) = 1.49 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: During calibration of a dielectric displacement gauge (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹), a 420 V supply charges parallel electrodes of area 0.7 m² spaced 4.00 × 10⁻⁴ m apart with relative permittivity 4. The electrodes are disconnected from the DC source so the plates remain electrically isolated, and the plate separation is then adjusted to 8.00 × 10⁻⁴ m at unchanged relative permittivity 4. What is the signed change in stored electrostatic energy ΔU = U_final − U_initial?
items.workedSolution: Initial C = 6.19 × 10⁻⁸ F and U_i = ½CV² = 5.46 × 10⁻³ J. Modified C′ = 3.10 × 10⁻⁸ F gives U_f = 0.0109 J, so ΔU = U_f − U_i = 5.46 × 10⁻³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Determines U_i and U_f under the isolated-charge constraint to obtain ΔU = 5.46 × 10⁻³ J (B).

items.stem: A 31 V DC power supply energises a series combination of capacitor C₁ = 15 μF and capacitor C₂ = 30 μF inside an avionics backup energy module. What potential difference is developed across capacitor C₁?
items.workedSolution: Equivalent capacitance C_eq = 1.00 × 10⁻⁵ F, so series charge Q = C_eq V₀ = 3.10 × 10⁻⁴ C. Across C₁, V₁ = Q / C₁ = 20.7 V.

markScheme.criterion: Finds common series charge Q and computes V₁ = Q/C₁ = 20.7 V (A).

items.stem: Within the evacuated auroral plasma simulation chamber, a perpendicular magnetic field of flux density 0.640 T (directed into the page) bends a proton (charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) travelling at 3.40 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. If the particle completes a semicircular turn to strike a flat detector wall on the entry plane, how far from the entry slit does it hit?
items.workedSolution: Cyclotron radius r = mv / (|q|B) = 0.0554 m. Across a semicircular turn, the impact distance from the entry slit equals the orbit diameter D = 2r = 0.111 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds r = mv/(|q|B) and doubles to diameter D = 2r = 0.111 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the curved semicircular arc length πr rather than the straight-line wall separation 2r.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Reports the cyclotron radius r instead of the semicircular chord diameter D = 2r along the detector wall.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the diameter a second time and reports 4r instead of 2r.

items.stem: Crossed fields in an accelerator monochromatic ion collimator are produced by 180 V across plates spaced 0.025 m apart (upper plate negative) and a 0.2 T field directed out of the page; a proton (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally to the right at 2.16 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. At what speed would a proton instead have to enter this same selector to pass straight through undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Electric field E = V / d = 180 / 0.025 = 7.20 × 10³ V m⁻¹. Undeflected transmission requires qvB = qE, giving v_sel = E / B = 3.60 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In the high-voltage surge filter shown between terminals A and B, capacitor C₁ = 50 μF is connected in series with the parallel pair C₂ = 60 μF and C₃ = 40 μF. Every capacitor has a maximum safe working voltage of 100 V. What is the maximum safe potential difference that can be applied across terminals A and B without exceeding the rating of any capacitor?
items.workedSolution: Parallel pair C_p = C₂ + C₃ = 100 μF. Because C₁ (50 μF) and C_p (100 μF) carry equal series charge Q, the smaller capacitance (single series capacitor) reaches 100 V first. Thus V_AB,max = 100 × (1 + 50 / 100) = 150.0 V ≈ 150 V.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies that the single series capacitor limits the voltage and calculates V_AB,max = 150 V.

items.stem: During a heart-pacemaker timing circuit test, switch S connects a pre-charged 20 μF capacitor (initial p.d. 12 V) across a 25 kΩ fixed resistor for an elapsed interval of 0.25 s. What is the potential difference across the capacitor at t = 0.25 s?
items.workedSolution: Time constant τ = RC = 0.500 s. For discharging, V_C(0.25 s) = 12 e^(−0.25/0.500) = 7.28 V.

markScheme.criterion: Finds τ = RC and evaluates V_C at t = 0.25 s to obtain 7.28 V (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the capacitor reaches or retains the full supply voltage V₀ instantaneously.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Applies the charging equation V₀(1 − e^(−t/RC)) instead of exponential discharge V₀e^(−t/RC).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides elapsed time t by half-time RC ln 2 instead of the RC time constant τ = RC in the exponent.

items.stem: In a hydroelectric micro-turbine alternator, a rectangular coil of 50 turns and cross-sectional area 0.01 m² rotates steadily at 20 Hz inside a uniform 0.14 T magnetic field, passing through maximum flux linkage at t = 0 and sampled at t = 0.00417 s. What is the peak emf ε₀ generated by the rotating coil?
items.workedSolution: Angular speed ω = 2πf = 2π(20) = 126 rad s⁻¹. Peak emf ε₀ = NBAω = 50 × 0.14 × 0.01 × 126 = 8.80 V.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes single-turn peak emf BAω and omits multiplying by N turns.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the amplitude and reports peak-to-peak emf 2ε₀ instead of peak emf ε₀.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes rotational frequency f directly into NBAω instead of angular speed ω = 2πf, omitting the 2π factor.

items.stem: Entering along the symmetry plane at 4.20 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹, a proton of charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg traverses a uniform transverse electric field created by 606 V across 0.075 m plates separated by 0.05 m in a synchrotron injector electrostatic kicker. What is the magnitude of the transverse deflection as the particle exits the plates?
items.workedSolution: Transit time t = L / v₀ = 0.075 / 4.20 × 10⁵ = 1.79 × 10⁻⁷ s. Transverse acceleration a_y = |q|V / (md) = 1.16 × 10¹² m s⁻². Deflection |Δy| = ½ a_y t² = 0.0185 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t = L/v₀, a_y = |q|V/(md), and |Δy| = ½a_y t² = 0.0185 m (C).
